sentences.zh: 凶禮二）

translations.literal: Mourning Rites Two)
translations.idiomatic: Mourning Rites Two)

sentences.zh: 皇太子皇子等喪儀親王以下及公主以下喪儀

translations.literal: Mourning rites for the crown prince, imperial sons, and the like; mourning rites for princes of the blood and below, and for princesses and below
translations.idiomatic: Mourning rites for the crown prince and imperial sons; mourning rites for princes of the blood and below, and for princesses and below

sentences.zh: 醇賢親王及福晉喪儀忌辰賜祭葬賜諡

translations.literal: Mourning rites for Prince Chunxian and his consort; anniversary sacrifices; bestowal of sacrificial offerings, burial honors, and posthumous titles
translations.idiomatic: Mourning rites for Prince Chunxian and his consort; anniversary sacrifices; grants of sacrificial rites, burial honors, and posthumous titles

sentences.zh: 外籓賜恤品官喪禮士庶人喪禮服制

translations.literal: Condolence grants in the outer domains; mourning rites for ranked officials; mourning rites for gentry and commoners; regulations of mourning dress
translations.idiomatic: Condolence grants in the outer domains; mourning rites for officials, gentry, and commoners; mourning dress regulations

sentences.zh: 皇太子皇子及皇子福晉喪儀皇太子喪儀，有清家法，不立儲貳。

translations.literal: Mourning rites for the crown prince, imperial sons, and consorts of imperial sons. As for mourning rites for the crown prince: under Qing household law the heir apparent is not established.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning rites for the crown prince, imperial sons, and consorts of imperial sons. Mourning rites for the crown prince: by Qing dynastic custom no heir apparent was formally installed.

sentences.zh: 至乾隆三年，皇次子永璉薨。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Qianlong reign, the second imperial son, Yonglian, died.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 3, the second imperial son Yonglian died.

sentences.zh: 高宗諭曰：「永璉為朕嫡子，雖未冊立，已定建儲大計，其典禮應視皇太子行。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor decreed: "Yonglian was my son by the empress; although he had not yet been enfeoffed as heir, the great plan to establish him as successor was already fixed; the rites should be observed as for a crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor decreed: "Yonglian was my son by the empress. Though he had not yet been installed as heir, the plan to make him successor was already settled; his funeral observances should follow those of a crown prince."

sentences.zh: 」禮臣奏言：「皇太子喪禮，會典未載。

translations.literal: " The rites officials memorialized: "Mourning rites for a crown prince are not recorded in the Collected Statutes."
translations.idiomatic: The rites officials memorialized: "Mourning rites for a crown prince are not recorded in the Collected Statutes."

sentences.zh: 舊制，沖齡薨，不成服。

translations.literal: Under the old regulations, when one died in infancy no mourning garments were worn.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations, when a child died in infancy no full mourning was observed.

sentences.zh: 今議，皇帝素服，輟朝七日。

translations.literal: It was now proposed that the emperor wear plain mourning dress and suspend court audiences for seven days.
translations.idiomatic: It was now proposed that the emperor wear plain mourning dress and suspend court for seven days.

sentences.zh: 若親臨奠醊，冠摘纓。

translations.literal: If he came in person to offer libations, he was to remove the tassels from his cap.
translations.idiomatic: If he came in person to offer libations, he was to remove the tassels from his cap.

sentences.zh: 典喪大臣、奏遣之王公暨皇太子侍從官咸成服，內務府佐領、內管領下護軍、驍騎校等成服，以六百人為率，並初祭日除。

translations.literal: The minister in charge of the funeral, the princes and nobles dispatched on memorial business, and all attendants of the crown prince were to don mourning dress; assistant commandants and chief stewards of the Imperial Household Department, the guards and adjutants under them, and the like were to don mourning dress at the rate of six hundred men, all to lay aside mourning on the day of the first sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The minister overseeing the funeral, princes and nobles sent on memorial business, and all the crown prince's attendants were to wear mourning; assistant commandants, chief stewards, guards, adjutants, and the like—about six hundred men in all—were likewise to mourn and lay aside mourning on the day of the first sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 直省官奉文日，咸摘冠纓素服三日，停嫁娶、輟音樂，京師四十日，外省半之。

translations.literal: On the day provincial officials received the document, all were to remove cap tassels and wear plain dress for three days, suspend weddings, and cease music; in the capital for forty days, in the provinces half that.
translations.idiomatic: When provincial officials received the document, all were to remove cap tassels and wear plain dress for three days, suspend weddings, and cease music—for forty days in the capital and half that in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 幼殤例無引幡，今請依雍正時懷親王喪儀，引幡仍用。

translations.literal: For early death in infancy there was normally no funeral banner; it was now requested that, following the mourning rites for Prince Huai in the Yongzheng reign, the banner still be used.
translations.idiomatic: Early death in infancy normally allowed no funeral banner; it was now requested that, following the mourning rites for Prince Huai under Yongzheng, the banner still be used.

sentences.zh: 外籓額駙、王、公、台吉、公主、福晉、郡主服內來京，男摘冠纓，女去首飾。

translations.literal: Imperial sons-in-law of the outer domains, princes, dukes, taiji, princesses, consorts, and commandery princesses who came to the capital while in mourning: men removed cap tassels, women removed head ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial sons-in-law of the outer domains, princes, dukes, taiji, princesses, consorts, and commandery princesses who came to the capital while in mourning were to have men remove cap tassels and women remove head ornaments.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮使臣素服七日。

translations.literal: Korean envoys wore plain dress for seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Korean envoys wore plain mourning dress for seven days.

sentences.zh: 金棺用桐木。

translations.literal: The gilt coffin was to be of paulownia wood.
translations.idiomatic: The gilt coffin was to be of paulownia wood.

sentences.zh: 」啟奠帝親祭酒，奉移親視送。

translations.literal: " At the opening of mourning the emperor offered wine in person and personally viewed the removal of the coffin for escort.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of mourning the emperor offered wine in person and personally viewed the removal of the coffin.

sentences.zh: 禮部長官祭轝。

translations.literal: The chief minister of rites sacrificed at the bier.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister of rites sacrificed at the funeral carriage.

sentences.zh: 初祭內外會集，帝至殯殿奠酒三爵，每奠眾一拜，是日除服薙髮。

translations.literal: At the first sacrifice the inner and outer courts assembled; the emperor came to the mourning hall and offered wine in three libations, and at each libation the assembly bowed once; on that day mourning was laid aside and the hair was cut.
translations.idiomatic: At the first sacrifice the inner and outer courts assembled; the emperor came to the mourning hall and offered three libations of wine, the assembly bowing once at each; on that day mourning was laid aside and the hair was cut.

sentences.zh: 將冊諡，先期遣告太廟後殿、奉先殿，諡曰端慧。

translations.literal: When he was to be given a posthumous title, envoys were dispatched beforehand to announce at the rear hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and at the Hall for Veneration of Ancestors; his posthumous title was Duanhui.
translations.idiomatic: Before investiture with a posthumous title, envoys were dispatched to announce at the rear hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and at the Hall for Veneration of Ancestors; his posthumous title was Duanhui.

sentences.zh: 禮成。

translations.literal: The rites were completed.
translations.idiomatic: The rites were completed.

sentences.zh: 禮部頒行各省，並牒朝鮮國王，文到率百官素服，軍民罷嫁娶、音樂各三日。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites promulgated this to all provinces and also sent a dispatch to the king of Korea; when the document arrived all officials wore plain dress, and soldiers and civilians suspended weddings and music for three days each.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites promulgated this to all provinces and dispatched notice to the king of Korea; on receipt all officials wore plain dress, and soldiers and civilians suspended weddings and music for three days.

sentences.zh: 八年，葬硃華山園寢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was buried in the garden mausoleum at Zhuhua Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was buried in the garden mausoleum at Zhuhua Mountain.

sentences.zh: 皇子喪儀，順治十五年，榮親王薨，治喪視親王加厚，葬黃花山園寢。

translations.literal: Mourning rites for imperial sons: in the fifteenth year of Shunzhi, Prince Rong died; the funeral was conducted with observances thicker than for a prince of the blood, and he was buried in the garden mausoleum at Huanghua Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning rites for imperial sons: in Shunzhi 15 Prince Rong died; the funeral exceeded princely observances, and he was buried in the garden mausoleum at Huanghua Mountain.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，定制，凡皇子殤，備小式硃棺，祔葬黃花山，唯開墓穴平葬，不封不樹。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign regulations were fixed: whenever an imperial son died in infancy, a small-style vermilion coffin was prepared and he was buried by attachment at Huanghua Mountain, only opening a grave pit for a level burial without mound or trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kangxi reign it was regulated that whenever an imperial son died in infancy a small vermilion coffin was prepared and he was buried by attachment at Huanghua Mountain in a level grave without mound or trees.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，皇八子福惠卒，帝輟朝，大內素服各三日，不祭神，詔用親王禮葬。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng, the eighth imperial son Fuhui died; the emperor suspended court; within the inner palace plain dress was worn for three days each, sacrifices to the gods were not performed, and an edict ordered burial by princely rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 6 the eighth imperial son Fuhui died; the emperor suspended court; the inner palace wore plain dress for three days and did not sacrifice to the gods, and an edict ordered burial by princely rites.

sentences.zh: 十三年，追封親王，諡曰懷。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was posthumously enfeoffed as prince and given the posthumous title Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was posthumously enfeoffed as prince with the posthumous title Huai.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年，皇子永琮甫二周薨，帝言：「建儲之意，朕雖默定，然未若端慧太子旨已封貯，喪儀應視皇子為優。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong, the imperial son Yongcong died at barely two years of age; the emperor said: "My intent to establish an heir, though fixed in silence, was not like that of the Duanhui Crown Prince, whose edict was already sealed in storage; the mourning rites should be preferred over those for an ordinary imperial son."
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 13 the imperial son Yongcong died at barely two; the emperor said: "Though I had silently fixed my intent to establish an heir, it was not like the Duanhui Crown Prince, whose edict was already sealed away; his mourning rites should exceed those for an ordinary imperial son."

sentences.zh: 」大祭親臨奠醊，諡悼敏，後追封哲親王。

translations.literal: " At the great sacrifice the emperor came in person to offer libations; his posthumous title was Daomin, and later he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: At the great sacrifice the emperor came in person to offer libations; his posthumous title was Daomin, and later he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Zhe.

sentences.zh: 越二年，皇長子永璜薨，金棺用杉木，其福晉及皇孫綿德等翦發去首飾，成服百日而除，素服二十七月。

translations.literal: Two years later the eldest imperial son Yonghuang died; the gilt coffin was of fir wood; his consort and the imperial grandson Miande and others cut their hair and removed head ornaments, wore mourning for a hundred days and then laid it aside, and wore plain dress for twenty-seven months.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the eldest imperial son Yonghuang died; the gilt coffin was of fir; his consort and the imperial grandson Miande and others cut their hair, removed ornaments, wore full mourning for a hundred days and plain dress for twenty-seven months.

sentences.zh: 成服王公大祭日除。

translations.literal: Princes and nobles who had worn mourning laid it aside on the day of the great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and nobles in mourning laid it aside on the day of the great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 禮部以第三日移殯，請輟朝三日，詔改五日，追封定親王，諡曰安。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites proposed moving the coffin on the third day and requested suspending court for three days; an edict changed this to five days; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Ding with the posthumous title An.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites proposed moving the coffin on the third day and suspending court for three days; an edict changed this to five; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Ding with the posthumous title An.

sentences.zh: 初祭、大祭並親臨奠醊。

translations.literal: At the first sacrifice and the great sacrifice the emperor came in person to offer libations.
translations.idiomatic: At the first sacrifice and the great sacrifice the emperor came in person to offer libations.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，皇三子永璋薨，詔用郡王例治喪，輟朝二日。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the third imperial son Yongzhang died; an edict ordered the funeral conducted by commandery-prince precedent and court suspended for two days.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the third imperial son Yongzhang died; an edict ordered the funeral by commandery-prince precedent with court suspended two days.

sentences.zh: 大內、宗室素服咸五日，不祭神。

translations.literal: Within the inner palace and the imperial clan plain dress was worn for five days each; sacrifices to the gods were not performed.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace and imperial clan wore plain dress for five days and did not sacrifice to the gods.

sentences.zh: 追封循郡王。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as commandery prince of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as commandery prince of Xun.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，皇十二子永璂薨，詔用宗室公例治喪。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year the twelfth imperial son Yongji died; an edict ordered the funeral conducted by the precedent for a clan duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year the twelfth imperial son Yongji died; an edict ordered the funeral by clan-duke precedent.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，追封貝勒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was posthumously enfeoffed as beile.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4 he was posthumously enfeoffed as beile.

sentences.zh: 道光十一年，皇長子奕緯薨，命依皇子例治喪。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Daoguang the eldest imperial son Yizhu died; he was ordered to be mourned by imperial-son precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 11 the eldest imperial son Yizhu died; he was ordered mourned by imperial-son precedent.

sentences.zh: 罷公主、福晉、命婦會集，園寢不建碑，追封貝勒，諡曰隱志。

translations.literal: Assembly of princesses, consorts, and titled ladies was discontinued; no stele was erected at the garden mausoleum; he was posthumously enfeoffed as beile with the posthumous title Yinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Assembly of princesses, consorts, and titled ladies was discontinued; no stele was erected at the garden mausoleum; he was posthumously enfeoffed as beile with the posthumous title Yinzhi.

sentences.zh: 三十年，晉封郡王。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was promoted to commandery prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was promoted to commandery prince.

sentences.zh: 皇子福晉喪，定制，親王世子、多羅郡王下及奉恩將軍、固倫公主、和碩福晉下及固山格格、奉恩將軍妻咸會集。

translations.literal: When a consort of an imperial son died, by regulation the heir of a prince of the blood, those below a duolan commandery prince and down to a bannerman receiving grace, gulun princesses, consorts below a heshuo princess and down to a gushan gege, and wives of bannermen receiving grace all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: When a consort of an imperial son died, by regulation the princely heir, those from duolan commandery prince down to bannermen receiving grace, gulun princesses, consorts from heshuo princess down to gushan gege, and wives of bannermen receiving grace all assembled.

sentences.zh: 朝供饌筵，午果筵。

translations.literal: Morning offerings of food tables; noon offerings of fruit tables.
translations.idiomatic: Morning offerings of food tables; noon offerings of fruit tables.

sentences.zh: 初祭引幡一，楮幣十二萬，饌筵二十五，羊十五，酒七尊，讀文致祭。

translations.literal: At the first sacrifice one funeral banner, a hundred and twenty thousand sheets of spirit money, twenty-five food tables, fifteen sheep, seven jars of wine, and a eulogy read at the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: At the first sacrifice: one funeral banner, a hundred and twenty thousand sheets of spirit money, twenty-five food tables, fifteen sheep, seven jars of wine, and a eulogy read at the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 繹則陳楮幣三千，饌筵十二，羊、酒各七。

translations.literal: On the day of continuation three thousand sheets of spirit money were displayed, twelve food tables, and seven sheep and seven jars of wine each.
translations.idiomatic: On the continuation day: three thousand sheets of spirit money, twelve food tables, and seven sheep and seven jars of wine.

sentences.zh: 百日、周年、四時致奠禮同。

translations.literal: Offerings at the hundredth day, the anniversary, and the four seasons followed the same rites.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings at the hundredth day, anniversary, and four seasons followed the same rites.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年，宣宗時為皇次子，其福晉鈕祜祿氏薨，帝命即日成服，初祭後除。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing, when the future Xuanzong was second imperial son, his consort of the Niohuru clan died; the emperor ordered mourning dress worn that same day and laid aside after the first sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 13, when the future Xuanzong was second imperial son, his consort of the Niohuru clan died; the emperor ordered mourning worn that day and laid aside after the first sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 未分府皇子福晉依親王福晉例，金棺、座罩皆紅色，以無儀仗，特賞金黃色座罩，儀仗仍視親王福晉例用，旗色用鑲白，著為令。

translations.literal: For a consort of an imperial son not yet given a separate establishment, the precedent for a princely consort applied: gilt coffin and canopy cover were all red; because there was no guard of honor, a golden-yellow canopy cover was specially granted, while guard of honor still followed princely-consort precedent, banner color bordered white—established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: For a consort of an imperial son not yet given a separate establishment, princely-consort precedent applied: gilt coffin and canopy were red; lacking a guard of honor, a golden-yellow canopy was specially granted while the guard still followed princely-consort precedent, with bordered-white banners—established as regulation.

sentences.zh: 道光七年，皇長子奕緯福晉瓜爾佳氏薨，罷內外齊集及豫往暫安處接迎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daoguang the consort of the eldest imperial son Yizhu, of the Guwalgiya clan, died; inner and outer assembly and the preliminary escort to the temporary resting place were discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 7 the consort of the eldest imperial son Yizhu, of the Guwalgiya clan, died; inner and outer assembly and the preliminary escort to the temporary resting place were discontinued.

sentences.zh: 十一年，追封貝勒夫人，諏吉遣官奉紙冊往殯所，讀文致祭。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year she was posthumously enfeoffed as wife of a beile; an auspicious day was chosen and an official was sent with a paper patent to the mourning place, a eulogy read at the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year she was posthumously enfeoffed as wife of a beile; an auspicious day was chosen and an official sent with a paper patent to the mourning place to read a eulogy at the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 親王暨福晉等喪儀順治九年，定親王喪聞，輟朝三日。

translations.literal: Mourning rites for princes of the blood and consorts and the like: in the ninth year of Shunzhi it was fixed that on report of a prince's death court was suspended three days.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning rites for princes of the blood and consorts: in Shunzhi 9 it was fixed that on report of a prince's death court was suspended three days.

sentences.zh: 世子、郡王二日。

translations.literal: For an heir, commandery prince: two days.
translations.idiomatic: For a princely heir or commandery prince: two days.

sentences.zh: 後改貝勒以下罷輟朝。

translations.literal: Later this was changed so that from beile downward suspension of court was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: Later this was changed: from beile downward court was no longer suspended.

sentences.zh: 斂具，親王至貝勒采棺，藉五層。

translations.literal: Burial equipment: from prince of the blood to beile, coffins of selected wood with five layers of padding.
translations.idiomatic: Burial equipment: from prince of the blood to beile, coffins of selected wood with five layers of padding.

sentences.zh: 貝子至輔國公棺同，藉三層。

translations.literal: From beizi to auxiliary state duke the coffin was the same, with three layers of padding.
translations.idiomatic: From beizi to auxiliary state duke the coffin was the same, with three layers of padding.

sentences.zh: 鎮國將軍以下硃棺，藉一層。

translations.literal: From banner commander of the state downward, vermilion coffins with one layer of padding.
translations.idiomatic: From banner commander of the state downward, vermilion coffins with one layer of padding.

sentences.zh: 初薨陳儀衛，鞍馬、散馬親王十五，世子、郡王各十四，貝勒各十三，貝子各十二，鎮國公各十，輔國公各八；

translations.literal: At the first report of death guard of honor was displayed: saddle horses and loose horses—fifteen for a prince of the blood, fourteen each for heir and commandery prince, thirteen each for beile, twelve each for beizi, ten each for banner duke of the state, eight each for auxiliary state duke;
translations.idiomatic: At first report of death guard of honor was displayed: saddle horses and loose horses—fifteen for a prince of the blood, fourteen each for heir and commandery prince, thirteen for beile, twelve for beizi, ten for banner duke of the state, eight for auxiliary state duke;

sentences.zh: 鎮國將軍鞭馬七，輔國將軍五，奉國將軍四，奉恩將軍三。

translations.literal: banner commander of the state seven whip horses, auxiliary state commander five, state commander receiving grace four, banner commander receiving grace three.
translations.idiomatic: banner commander of the state seven whip horses, auxiliary state commander five, state commander receiving grace four, banner commander receiving grace three.

sentences.zh: 府屬內外咸成服，大祭日除。

translations.literal: Within and outside the establishment all wore mourning, laid aside on the day of the great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Within and outside the establishment all wore mourning, laid aside on the day of the great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 內外去冠飾、素服會集，各如其例。

translations.literal: Within and outside, cap ornaments removed and plain dress worn at assembly, each according to his precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Within and outside, cap ornaments were removed and plain dress worn at assembly, each according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 鎮國將軍以下不會喪。

translations.literal: From banner commander of the state downward they did not assemble for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: From banner commander of the state downward they did not assemble for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 公主、福晉、命婦會喪，臨時請旨行。

translations.literal: Assembly of princesses, consorts, and titled ladies for the funeral was carried out on imperial order when the occasion arose.
translations.idiomatic: Assembly of princesses, consorts, and titled ladies was ordered on imperial command when the occasion arose.

sentences.zh: 凡親王至輔國公，御祭二，遣官至墳讀文致祭。

translations.literal: For all from prince of the blood to auxiliary state duke, two imperial sacrifices; officials were dispatched to the tomb to read a eulogy at the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: For all from prince of the blood to auxiliary state duke there were two imperial sacrifices; officials were dispatched to the tomb to read a eulogy.

sentences.zh: 宗人府請賜諡，撰給碑文。

translations.literal: The Court of the Imperial Clan requested bestowal of a posthumous title and composition and grant of an epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of the Imperial Clan requested a posthumous title and composition and grant of an epitaph.

sentences.zh: 工部樹碑建亭，貝勒以下碑自建，給葬費有差。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Works erected stele and pavilion; from beile downward the stele was erected by the family; burial expenses were granted in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Works erected stele and pavilion; from beile downward the family erected the stele; burial expenses were granted in differing amounts.

sentences.zh: 鎮國將軍至奉國將軍賜祭二，文一。

translations.literal: From banner commander of the state to state commander receiving grace, two sacrifices were granted, one with a written eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: From banner commander of the state to state commander receiving grace, two sacrifices were granted, one with a written eulogy.

sentences.zh: 立碑、予諡，臨時請旨。

translations.literal: Erection of stele and grant of posthumous title were requested on imperial order when the occasion arose.
translations.idiomatic: Erection of stele and grant of posthumous title were requested on imperial command when the occasion arose.

sentences.zh: 奉恩將軍賜祭無文，不立碑，不予諡。

translations.literal: For a banner commander receiving grace, sacrifices were granted without a written eulogy; no stele was erected and no posthumous title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: For a banner commander receiving grace, sacrifices were granted without a written eulogy; no stele was erected and no posthumous title granted.

sentences.zh: 王至公婚娶之子卒，許陳鞍馬，祭品各如其父母例，唯不遣官致祭。

translations.literal: When a son of a prince or duke down to a gong who had married died, saddle horses might be displayed and sacrificial offerings each followed the precedent for his parents, only no official was dispatched to sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When a married son of a prince, duke, or gong died, saddle horses might be displayed and offerings followed his parents' precedent, but no official was dispatched to sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 未婚娶幼子不造墳。

translations.literal: An unmarried young son had no tomb built.
translations.idiomatic: An unmarried young son had no tomb built.

sentences.zh: 凡葬期，親王期年，郡王七月，貝子以下五月。

translations.literal: As for burial periods: prince of the blood one year, commandery prince seven months, beizi and below five months.
translations.idiomatic: Burial periods: prince of the blood one year, commandery prince seven months, beizi and below five months.

sentences.zh: 又定親王福晉以下喪，內外會集如制，陳儀衛從其封爵，親王福晉、側福晉、世子福晉御祭一。

translations.literal: It was further fixed that for death from a princely consort downward, inner and outer assembly followed regulation, guard of honor displayed according to enfeoffment; for a princely consort, secondary consort, and heir's consort, one imperial sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: For death from a princely consort downward, inner and outer assembly followed regulation and guard of honor matched enfeoffment; a princely consort, secondary consort, or heir's consort received one imperial sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 十二年，定下嫁外籓公主喪，御祭一，遣官至塋所讀文致祭。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year it was fixed that for death of a princess married to the outer domains, one imperial sacrifice; an official was dispatched to the burial place to read a eulogy at the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year it was fixed that for a princess married to the outer domains there was one imperial sacrifice; an official was dispatched to the burial place to read a eulogy.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，定貝勒至入八分公予諡請旨行。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi it was fixed that from beile to gong entered in the eight banners, grant of posthumous title was on imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 4 it was fixed that from beile to gong entered in the eight banners, posthumous titles required imperial order.

sentences.zh: 九年，定親王至輔國公喪，本府官屬具喪服，其禮親王、肅親王、承澤親王、敬謹親王、饒餘親王、鄭親王、克勤郡王、恪僖貝勒、靖寧貝勒、顧爾馬洪貝子、福勒黑公十二支，凡為本支所分者，本身暨府屬官、命婦咸具喪服，非本支會喪者摘冠纓，從官如其主，尊屬無服。

translations.literal: In the ninth year it was fixed that for death from prince of the blood to auxiliary state duke, officials of the establishment wore mourning; the rites for the twelve branches—Prince of the Blood Su, Prince of the Blood Chengze, Prince of the Blood Jingjin, Prince of the Blood Raoyu, Prince of Zheng, Prince of Keqin, Beile Kexi, Beile Jingning, Beizi Guermahong, and Gong Fulehei—for all apportioned to a branch, the person himself and establishment officials and titled ladies all wore mourning; those of other branches assembling for the funeral removed cap tassels, retainers following their master, senior kin without mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year it was fixed that for death from prince of the blood to auxiliary state duke, establishment officials wore mourning; for the twelve branches—Su, Chengze, Jingjin, Raoyu, Zheng, Keqin, Kexi, Jingning, Guermahong, Fulehei, and the like—all apportioned to a branch wore full mourning themselves and as establishment officials and titled ladies; other branches assembling removed cap tassels, retainers following their masters, senior kin without mourning.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，定貝勒生母薨，治喪如嫡夫人，遣官讀文致祭。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year it was fixed that when a beile's birth mother died, the funeral was conducted like that for the principal wife and an official was dispatched to read a eulogy at the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year it was fixed that when a beile's birth mother died, the funeral followed the principal wife and an official read a eulogy at the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，定固倫公主有子孫者，獲請建碑予諡。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year it was fixed that a gulun princess who had descendants might request erection of stele and grant of posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year it was fixed that a gulun princess with descendants might request a stele and posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，遵旨議定嗣後皇帝子孫依五等服制，遇期服伯叔兄弟喪，依例具奏臨喪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, following an imperial order it was deliberated and fixed that thereafter imperial sons and grandsons, following the five grades of mourning, when encountering mourning for uncles and brothers in the one-year grade, should memorialize and attend the funeral according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4, following imperial order it was fixed that thereafter imperial sons and grandsons, under the five grades of mourning, when uncles and brothers in the one-year grade died should memorialize and attend according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 其諸王以下，不論爵次，遇小功以上喪，會喪成服，期六十日、大功一月、小功七日除。

translations.literal: For all princes and below, regardless of rank, when encountering mourning above the five-day grade, they assembled for the funeral and wore mourning: one-year grade sixty days, nine-month grade one month, five-day grade seven days to lay aside.
translations.idiomatic: For all princes and below, regardless of rank, when mourning above the five-day grade occurred they assembled and wore mourning: one-year grade sixty days, nine-month grade one month, five-day grade seven days to lay aside.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，更定期服大祭日、大功初祭日、小功送殯日除。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong it was further fixed: one-year grade on the day of the great sacrifice, nine-month grade on the day of the first sacrifice, five-day grade on the day of escorting the coffin to lay aside mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 3 it was further fixed: one-year grade on the great-sacrifice day, nine-month on the first-sacrifice day, five-day on the escort day to lay aside mourning.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，諭諸王側福晉予諡請旨行，予祭不逾一次，罷給祭文。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year an edict ordered that posthumous titles for secondary consorts of princes required imperial approval; sacrifices granted not more than once; grant of sacrificial eulogies discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year an edict ordered posthumous titles for princes' secondary consorts required imperial approval; sacrifices not more than once; sacrificial eulogies discontinued.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，定貝勒、貝子、公兼一品職獲請予諡，鎮國暨輔國將軍兼一品職獲請賜恤。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year it was fixed that beile, beizi, and gong who also held first-rank office might request posthumous title; banner commanders and auxiliary state commanders who also held first-rank office might request condolence grants.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year it was fixed that beile, beizi, and gong holding first-rank office might request posthumous title; banner and auxiliary state commanders holding first-rank office might request condolence grants.

sentences.zh: 四十年，定凡側福晉為王等生母，獲請賜祭，降嫡福晉一等。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year it was fixed that whenever a secondary consort was birth mother of a prince or the like, sacrificial grants might be requested, one grade below the principal consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year it was fixed that when a secondary consort was birth mother of a prince or the like, sacrificial grants might be requested one grade below the principal consort.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，鎮國公晉昌夫人卒，詔罷賜祭，後仿此。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year the wife of Banner Duke Jinchang of the State died; an edict discontinued sacrificial grants; later cases followed this.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year the wife of Banner Duke Jinchang died; an edict discontinued sacrificial grants, and later cases followed.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十七年，貝勒綿懃子奕綬卒，命封為未入八分輔國公，嗣後宗室如追封公，俱作為未入八分，著為令。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Jiaqing, when the son of Beile Mianqin, Yishou, died, he was ordered enfeoffed as auxiliary state duke not entered in the eight banners; thereafter when the imperial clan was posthumously enfeoffed as gong, all were treated as not entered in the eight banners—established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 17 when Beile Mianqin's son Yishou died, he was ordered enfeoffed as auxiliary state duke not entered in the eight banners; thereafter posthumous enfeoffment as gong in the imperial clan was all treated as not entered in the eight banners—established as regulation.

sentences.zh: 公主以下喪儀，順治九年，定固倫公主喪視親王福晉，和碩公主視世子福晉，郡主視郡王福晉，縣主視貝勒夫人，郡君視貝子夫人，縣君視鎮國公夫人。

translations.literal: Mourning rites for princesses and below: in the ninth year of Shunzhi it was fixed that mourning for a gulun princess followed that for a princely consort, heshuo princess for an heir's consort, commandery princess for a commandery-prince consort, district princess for a beile's wife, commandery lady for a beizi's wife, district lady for a banner duke's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning rites for princesses and below: in Shunzhi 9 mourning for a gulun princess followed a princely consort, heshuo an heir's consort, commandery princess a commandery-prince consort, district princess a beile's wife, commandery lady a beizi's wife, district lady a banner duke's wife.

sentences.zh: 十二年，定下嫁外籓公主至縣主並給諭祭文，遣官赴墳讀奠。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year it was fixed that for princesses married to the outer domains down to district princesses, an edict and sacrificial eulogy were granted and an official was sent to the tomb to read and offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year it was fixed that for princesses married to the outer domains down to district princesses, an edict and sacrificial eulogy were granted and an official sent to the tomb to read and sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 郡君以下，致祭無文。

translations.literal: For commandery lady and below, sacrifice was offered without a written eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: For commandery lady and below, sacrifice was offered without a written eulogy.

sentences.zh: 道光二十四年，定公主薨，內務府請旨，如命官為治喪，一切典禮，即會禮部具奏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang it was fixed that when a princess died, the Imperial Household Department requested imperial order; if officials were ordered to conduct the funeral, all ceremonies were jointly memorialized by the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 24 it was fixed that when a princess died the Imperial Household Department requested imperial order; if officials were ordered to conduct the funeral, all ceremonies were jointly memorialized by the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 得旨，再牒各署治辦，額駙自行治喪，禮部應將會集處奏聞。

translations.literal: When the order was received, dispatches were again sent to each office to arrange matters; the imperial son-in-law conducted the funeral himself; the Ministry of Rites was to memorialize the place of assembly.
translations.idiomatic: When the order was received, each office was again instructed to arrange matters; the imperial son-in-law conducted the funeral; the Ministry of Rites memorialized the place of assembly.

sentences.zh: 公主以下喪，會集臨時請旨，如獲請，牒宗人府、五旗傳行。

translations.literal: For death of princesses and below, assembly was requested on imperial order when the occasion arose; if granted, dispatches were sent to the Court of the Imperial Clan and the Five Banners for transmission.
translations.idiomatic: For princesses and below, assembly was requested on imperial command; if granted, the Court of the Imperial Clan and Five Banners were notified.

sentences.zh: 未釐降受封者，內務府治喪，不會集。

translations.literal: Those enfeoffed before demarcation of descent wore mourning conducted by the Imperial Household Department without assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Those enfeoffed before demarcation of descent were mourned by the Imperial Household Department without assembly.

sentences.zh: 醇賢親王及福晉喪儀光緒十六年，醇親王奕枻薨，定稱號曰「皇帝本生考」，帝持服期年，縞素十有一日，輟朝如之。

translations.literal: Mourning rites for Prince Chunxian and his consort: in the sixteenth year of Guangxu, Prince Chun Yi died; his title was fixed as "the Emperor's biological father"; the emperor wore mourning for one year, plain white for eleven days, and court was suspended likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning rites for Prince Chunxian and his consort: in Guangxu 16 Prince Chun Yi died; his title was fixed as "the Emperor's biological father"; the emperor mourned one year, wore plain white eleven days, and suspended court likewise.

sentences.zh: 期年內御便殿仍素服。

translations.literal: Within the one-year period he still wore plain dress in the informal palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: Within the one-year period he still wore plain dress in the informal palace hall.

sentences.zh: 元旦謁堂子，詣慈寧宮，太和殿受朝，並禮服。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day he worshipped at the Tangzi, went to the Cining Palace, and received congratulations in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, all in ceremonial dress.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day he worshipped at the Tangzi, went to the Cining Palace, and received congratulations in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, all in ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 唯升殿不宣表，樂設不作，罷宗親、廷臣筵宴。

translations.literal: Only when ascending the hall the proclamation was not read, music was set out but not performed, and banquets for imperial kin and court ministers were discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: Only on ascending the hall the proclamation was not read, music was prepared but not performed, and banquets for imperial kin and court ministers were discontinued.

sentences.zh: 祭文、碑文書皇帝名。

translations.literal: Sacrificial texts and stele inscriptions bore the emperor's name.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial texts and stele inscriptions bore the emperor's name.

sentences.zh: 初祭、大祭暨奉移園寢並御青袍褂，冠摘纓，親詣行禮。

translations.literal: At the first sacrifice, great sacrifice, and escorting to the garden mausoleum, the emperor wore blue robe and jacket, removed cap tassels, and came in person to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the first sacrifice, great sacrifice, and escort to the garden mausoleum, the emperor wore blue robe and jacket, removed cap tassels, and came in person to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 又定廟制及祭葬，廟中殿宇及正門瓦色，中用黃琉璃，殿脊及正門四圍用綠琉璃。

translations.literal: It was further fixed for temple regulations and sacrificial burial: within the temple, hall roof tiles and main gate tiles used yellow glazed in the middle, and green glazed on hall ridges and on the four sides around the main gate.
translations.idiomatic: Temple and burial regulations were further fixed: hall and main-gate tiles used yellow glaze in the center and green glaze on the ridges and around the main gate.

sentences.zh: 祀以天子禮。

translations.literal: Sacrifice followed Son of Heaven rites.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice followed Son of Heaven rites.

sentences.zh: 歲時饗，四仲月朔舉行，忌辰躬親致祭。

translations.literal: Seasonal offerings were held on the first day of the four mid-season months; on the anniversary the emperor came in person to sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal offerings were held on the first day of each mid-season month; on the anniversary the emperor sacrificed in person.

sentences.zh: 葬以親王禮，帝親制碑文，諡曰賢。

translations.literal: Burial followed princely rites; the emperor composed the stele inscription in person; his posthumous title was Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Burial followed princely rites; the emperor composed the stele inscription; his posthumous title was Xian.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，其福晉葉赫那拉氏薨，稱「皇帝本生妣」，喪儀如醇賢親王例。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year his consort of the Yehe Nara clan died; she was styled "the Emperor's biological mother"; mourning rites followed the precedent for Prince Chunxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year his consort of the Yehe Nara clan died; she was styled "the Emperor's biological mother"; mourning followed Prince Chunxian's precedent.

sentences.zh: 忌辰順治十年，定盛京、興京三陵忌辰，遣守陵官行禮，獻酒果，不讀祝，不奠帛。

translations.literal: Anniversary sacrifices: in the tenth year of Shunzhi it was fixed that on the anniversaries of the three mausoleums at Shengjing and Xingjing, tomb-guard officials performed the rites, offering wine and fruit, without reading prayers or offering silks.
translations.idiomatic: Anniversary sacrifices: in Shunzhi 10 anniversaries of the three mausoleums at Shengjing and Xingjing were fixed; tomb-guard officials performed the rites with wine and fruit, without reading prayers or offering silks.

sentences.zh: 十二年，改定忌辰遣官，禮部具題請旨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year it was changed that officials dispatched for anniversary sacrifices were memorialized by the Ministry of Rites for imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year dispatch of officials for anniversary sacrifices was changed to require memorialization by the Ministry of Rites for imperial order.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，復定三陵忌辰在隆恩殿神牌前揭幔致祭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi it was again fixed that anniversaries of the three mausoleums were offered before the spirit tablets in the Hall of Imperial Grace with the curtain drawn aside.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3 it was again fixed that the three mausoleums' anniversaries were offered before the spirit tablets in the Hall of Imperial Grace with the curtain drawn aside.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，帝以聖祖喪滿，哀慕無窮，思依三年內祭禮舉行，下禮臣議。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, as the emperor's mourning for the Sagely Ancestor was complete yet grief was boundless, he wished to follow the sacrificial rites within the three-year period and ordered the rites officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4, with mourning for Kangxi complete but grief unbounded, the emperor wished to follow three-year mourning sacrifices and ordered rites officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 尋議上，依周年祭祀例，遣在京或陵寢王公大臣一人承祭，在京王公百官遣三之一陪祭。

translations.literal: Shortly the deliberation was submitted: following the precedent for anniversary sacrifices, one prince or grand minister at the capital or mausoleum was dispatched to preside; at the capital one-third of princes and officials were dispatched to assist.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberation was soon submitted: following anniversary-sacrifice precedent, one prince or grand minister at capital or mausoleum presided; at the capital one-third of princes and officials assisted.

sentences.zh: 著為令。

translations.literal: Established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Established as regulation.

sentences.zh: 十三年，高宗嗣服，議定聖祖忌辰，依陵寢四時大祭，用太牢，獻帛爵，讀祝文，遣官承祭，陵寢官悉陪祀，罷遣京官往。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the Gaozong succeeded to mourning, it was deliberated and fixed that on the Sagely Ancestor's anniversary, following the four-season great sacrifices at the mausoleum, a full ox was used, silks and libation cups offered, prayers read, an official dispatched to preside, all mausoleum officials assisting; dispatch of capital officials was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when Qianlong succeeded, the Sagely Ancestor's anniversary was fixed to follow mausoleum four-season great sacrifices with full ox, silks, libation cups, and prayers; an official presided with all mausoleum officials assisting; capital officials were no longer dispatched.

sentences.zh: 嗣後列聖、列後忌辰，永如例行。

translations.literal: Thereafter anniversaries of successive emperors and empresses followed this precedent permanently.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter anniversaries of successive emperors and empresses followed this precedent permanently.

sentences.zh: 定制，帝、後忌辰，內外俱素服，停宴會，輟音樂，不理刑名，帝詣奉先殿後殿上香行禮。

translations.literal: By regulation, on the anniversaries of emperor and empress, inner and outer courts all wore plain dress, banquets were discontinued, music ceased, criminal cases were not handled, and the emperor went to the rear hall of the Hall for Veneration of Ancestors to offer incense and perform rites.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation, on emperor and empress anniversaries all wore plain dress, banquets and music ceased, criminal cases were not handled, and the emperor offered incense at the rear hall of the Hall for Veneration of Ancestors.

sentences.zh: 如祀南郊，帝閱祝版，遇忌辰，御龍袍、龍褂、掛數珠，執事官蟒服、補褂、掛數珠。

translations.literal: When sacrificing at the Southern Suburb, the emperor reviewed prayer boards; on an anniversary he wore dragon robe, dragon jacket, and prayer beads; officiants wore python-pattern dress, rank-patch jacket, and prayer beads.
translations.idiomatic: When sacrificing at the Southern Suburb the emperor reviewed prayer boards; on an anniversary he wore dragon robe and jacket with prayer beads; officiants wore python dress, rank-patch jacket, and prayer beads.

sentences.zh: 閱北郊、廟社暨各中祀祝版，則俱御龍褂、掛數珠，執事官咸補服、掛數珠。

translations.literal: When reviewing prayer boards for the Northern Suburb, temple and altar, and all middle sacrifices, he wore dragon jacket and prayer beads; officiants all wore rank-patch dress and prayer beads.
translations.idiomatic: For Northern Suburb, temple, altar, and middle sacrifices he wore dragon jacket and prayer beads; officiants wore rank-patch dress and prayer beads.

sentences.zh: 大祀齋期內，御常服、掛數珠，陪祀執事官亦如之。

translations.literal: Within the abstention period of a great sacrifice he wore ordinary dress and prayer beads; assisting and officiating officials likewise.
translations.idiomatic: During great-sacrifice abstention he wore ordinary dress and prayer beads; assisting and officiating officials likewise.

sentences.zh: 凡祭日遇忌辰，行禮時祭服作樂，禮畢仍素服。

translations.literal: Whenever a sacrifice day fell on an anniversary, sacrificial dress and music were used during the rites; when the rites were complete plain dress was resumed.
translations.idiomatic: When a sacrifice day fell on an anniversary, sacrificial dress and music were used during the rites; afterward plain dress resumed.

sentences.zh: 賜祭葬世祖初入關，沿崇德間例，超品公，一、二、三等公卒，遣官祭三次；

translations.literal: Bestowal of sacrificial rites and burial: when the Shizu first entered the Pass, following the Chongde precedent, for super-rank dukes and first-, second-, and third-rank dukes who died, officials were dispatched to sacrifice three times;
translations.idiomatic: Bestowal of sacrifice and burial: when Shunzhi first entered the Pass, following Chongde precedent, super-rank and first-, second-, and third-rank dukes received three official sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 子、副都統二次；

translations.literal: for sons and vice commanders-in-chief, twice;
translations.idiomatic: for sons and vice commanders-in-chief, twice;

sentences.zh: 參領、佐領一次。

translations.literal: for battalion commanders and assistant commandants, once.
translations.idiomatic: for battalion commanders and assistant commandants, once.

sentences.zh: 陣亡與有勛勞者，遣官治喪，出自上裁。

translations.literal: For those killed in battle or with meritorious service, officials conducted the funeral at the emperor's discretion.
translations.idiomatic: For those killed in battle or with merit, officials conducted the funeral at imperial discretion.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，定制民公、侯、伯、子兼任內大臣、都統、大學士、尚書、鎮守將軍卒，候旨立碑，致祭一次。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi it was fixed that when civilian dukes, marquises, earls, and viscounts who also served as inner grand ministers, commanders-in-chief, grand secretaries, ministers, or garrison generals died, a stele was erected on imperial order and sacrifice offered once.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3 it was fixed that civilian dukes, marquises, earls, and viscounts also serving as inner grand ministers, commanders-in-chief, grand secretaries, ministers, or garrison generals received an imperial-order stele and one sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 襲公、侯、伯、子在任不逾三年，止給祭品，無祭文，不立碑。

translations.literal: Heirs to dukes, marquises, earls, and viscounts in office less than three years received only sacrificial offerings, no sacrificial eulogy, and no stele.
translations.idiomatic: Heirs in office less than three years received offerings only, no eulogy, and no stele.

sentences.zh: 二、三品官卒，給祭品。

translations.literal: When second- and third-rank officials died, sacrificial offerings were granted.
translations.idiomatic: When second- and third-rank officials died, sacrificial offerings were granted.

sentences.zh: 滿任三年給祭文。

translations.literal: After three full years of service a sacrificial eulogy was granted.
translations.idiomatic: After three full years a sacrificial eulogy was granted.

sentences.zh: 有戰功者，獲請立碑。

translations.literal: Those with military merit might request erection of a stele.
translations.idiomatic: Those with military merit might request a stele.

sentences.zh: 十三年，定佐領、員外郎、主事任滿三年，給祭品、祭文，未滿者無祭文。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year it was fixed that assistant commandants, outer-court secretaries, and clerks after three full years received offerings and eulogy; if not full, no eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year assistant commandants, outer-court secretaries, and clerks after three years received offerings and eulogy; if not full, no eulogy.

sentences.zh: 致仕同。

translations.literal: Retired officials were treated the same.
translations.idiomatic: Retired officials were treated the same.

sentences.zh: 十五年，定部、院長官加秩至一、二品，致祭、立碑。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year it was fixed that when heads of ministries and courts were promoted to first or second rank, sacrifice and stele were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year ministry and court heads promoted to first or second rank received sacrifice and stele.

sentences.zh: 三品滿三年者如之。

translations.literal: Third rank after three full years was treated likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank after three years was treated likewise.

sentences.zh: 未滿，但致祭而已。

translations.literal: If not full, only sacrifice was granted.
translations.idiomatic: If not full, only sacrifice was granted.

sentences.zh: 護軍統領、副都統、前鋒統領、步軍總尉考滿視三品。

translations.literal: Banner guard commanders, vice commanders-in-chief, vanguard commanders, and infantry commanders after examination for full tenure were treated as third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Banner guard commanders, vice commanders-in-chief, vanguard commanders, and infantry commanders after full tenure were treated as third rank.

sentences.zh: 如為男爵，得致祭、立碑。

translations.literal: If holding baron rank, sacrifice and stele might be granted.
translations.idiomatic: If holding baron rank, sacrifice and stele might be granted.

sentences.zh: 參領、前鋒參領滿三年，致祭，不立碑。

translations.literal: Battalion commanders and vanguard battalion commanders after three full years received sacrifice but no stele.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion and vanguard battalion commanders after three years received sacrifice but no stele.

sentences.zh: 四品卿、少卿考滿者同，否則不給祭文。

translations.literal: Fourth-rank directors and vice directors after examination were treated likewise; otherwise no eulogy was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth-rank directors and vice directors after examination were treated likewise; otherwise no eulogy.

sentences.zh: 陣亡不論品級，獲請恩恤。

translations.literal: Those killed in battle regardless of rank might request gracious condolence.
translations.idiomatic: Those killed in battle regardless of rank might request gracious condolence.

sentences.zh: 內大臣、都統、大學士、尚書、護軍統領、副都統、前鋒統領、侍郎、學士、步軍總尉原品休致者，致祭、立碑同。

translations.literal: Inner grand ministers, commanders-in-chief, grand secretaries, ministers, banner guard commanders, vice commanders-in-chief, vanguard commanders, vice ministers, academicians, and infantry commanders who retired at original rank received sacrifice and stele likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Inner grand ministers, commanders-in-chief, grand secretaries, ministers, banner guard commanders, vice commanders-in-chief, vanguard commanders, vice ministers, academicians, and infantry commanders retired at original rank received sacrifice and stele likewise.

sentences.zh: 現任輕車都尉、佐領、騎都尉、郎中、員外郎、主事，致祭、無碑文。

translations.literal: Serving chariot commanders of the third rank, assistant commandants, commanders of the fourth rank, directors, outer-court secretaries, and clerks received sacrifice without stele inscription.
translations.idiomatic: Serving chariot commanders of the third rank, assistant commandants, commanders of the fourth rank, directors, outer-court secretaries, and clerks received sacrifice without stele.

sentences.zh: 承襲公、侯、伯有職任者，依職任予恤，否則止給祭品。

translations.literal: Heirs to dukes, marquises, and earls with office received condolence according to office; otherwise only offerings were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Heirs with office received condolence by office; otherwise only offerings.

sentences.zh: 十七年，定本身所得民公、侯、伯、子及都統有職任內大臣、鎮守將軍給全葬。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year it was fixed that civilian dukes, marquises, earls, and viscounts personally received and commanders-in-chief serving as inner grand ministers or garrison generals received full burial.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year civilian dukes, marquises, earls, and viscounts personally received and commanders-in-chief as inner grand ministers or garrison generals received full burial.

sentences.zh: 大學士，尚書，左、右都御史加級及宮保者，視一品給全葬，無加銜、加級視二品給全葬。

translations.literal: Grand secretaries, ministers, censors promoted in rank and palace guardians were treated as first rank for full burial; without additional title or promotion, as second rank for full burial.
translations.idiomatic: Grand secretaries, ministers, promoted censors, and palace guardians received first-rank full burial; without additional title or promotion, second-rank full burial.

sentences.zh: 侍郎無兼銜、加級而考滿者，視三品給全葬，未滿者半之。

translations.literal: Vice ministers without additional title or promotion who had completed examination received third-rank full burial; if not full, half.
translations.idiomatic: Vice ministers without additional title who completed examination received third-rank full burial; if not full, half.

sentences.zh: 四品卿、少卿或兼少卿銜，視四品，止給祭品。

translations.literal: Fourth-rank directors and vice directors or those with vice director title were treated as fourth rank and received only offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth-rank directors and vice directors received only offerings.

sentences.zh: 護軍統領、前鋒統領、副都統、步軍總尉任滿給全葬，未滿者半之，並致祭一次。

translations.literal: Banner guard commanders, vanguard commanders, vice commanders-in-chief, and infantry commanders after full tenure received full burial; if not full, half, and sacrifice once.
translations.idiomatic: Banner guard, vanguard, vice commander, and infantry commanders after full tenure received full burial; if not full, half, and one sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 武職自參領、文職自郎中以下，俱不給祭品。

translations.literal: From military battalion commanders and civil directors downward, no offerings were granted.
translations.idiomatic: From military battalion commanders and civil directors downward, no offerings.

sentences.zh: 陣亡者如故。

translations.literal: Those killed in battle were treated as before.
translations.idiomatic: Those killed in battle were treated as before.

sentences.zh: 十八年，定本身所得民公、侯、伯造葬，致祭一次，加祭出特恩。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year it was fixed that civilian dukes, marquises, and earls personally received were granted burial construction and sacrifice once; additional sacrifice was special grace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year civilian dukes, marquises, and earls personally received received burial construction and one sacrifice; additional sacrifice was special grace.

sentences.zh: 都統、內大臣、大學士、尚書、右都御史、子、鎮守將軍及加銜、加級至一二品官，俱依品級造葬，致祭一次。

translations.literal: Commanders-in-chief, inner grand ministers, grand secretaries, ministers, right censors, viscounts, garrison generals, and officials with additional titles or promotions to first or second rank all received burial by rank and sacrifice once.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders-in-chief, inner grand ministers, grand secretaries, ministers, right censors, viscounts, garrison generals, and officials with titles or promotions to first or second rank received burial by rank and one sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 三品侍郎、學士、通政使、大理寺卿考滿者給全葬，未滿者半之，俱致祭一次。

translations.literal: Third-rank vice ministers, academicians, communications commissioners, and chief judges after examination received full burial; if not full, half; all received sacrifice once.
translations.idiomatic: Third-rank vice ministers, academicians, communications commissioners, and chief judges after examination received full burial; if not full, half; all one sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 參領、協領、郎中、佐領及三等侍衛、護衛官陣亡者，致祭一次。

translations.literal: Battalion commanders, assistant commandants, directors, assistant commandants, and third-rank bodyguards and guards killed in battle received sacrifice once.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion commanders, assistant commandants, directors, assistant commandants, and third-rank guards killed in battle received one sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 漢文職一、二品或三品考滿，俱致祭、造葬，未滿者半之，致祭一次。

translations.literal: Han civil officials of first or second rank or third rank after examination all received sacrifice and burial construction; if not full, half and sacrifice once.
translations.idiomatic: Han civil officials of first, second, or third rank after examination received sacrifice and burial; if not full, half and one sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 在外布、按以上，依京秩例行。

translations.literal: Provincial governors and censors and above followed capital rank precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governors and censors and above followed capital precedent.

sentences.zh: 武職加銜副將以上，造葬，致祭一次，無兼銜而考滿者同，未滿者半之，致祭一次。

translations.literal: Military officials with additional title of vice general and above received burial construction and sacrifice once; without additional title but after examination, likewise; if not full, half and sacrifice once.
translations.idiomatic: Military officials with vice-general title and above received burial and one sacrifice; without title but after examination likewise; if not full, half and one sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 知縣、守備以上陣亡者，各依加贈品級造葬，致祭一次。

translations.literal: Magistrates, garrison commanders, and above killed in battle each received burial by posthumously granted rank and sacrifice once.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates, garrison commanders, and above killed in battle received burial by posthumous rank and one sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 凡滿、漢文武原官致仕者，恤典同現任。

translations.literal: All Manchu and Han civil and military officials who retired at original rank received condolence like incumbents.
translations.idiomatic: All Manchu and Han officials retired at original rank received condolence like incumbents.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，定本身所得及承襲公、侯、伯給全葬，遣官讀文，致祭一次。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi it was fixed that dukes, marquises, and earls personally received or by inheritance received full burial; an official was dispatched to read the eulogy and sacrifice once.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 9 dukes, marquises, and earls personally or by inheritance received full burial; an official read the eulogy and sacrificed once.

sentences.zh: 內大臣、都統、子品級散秩大臣、大學士、尚書、左都御史、子、世襲子、鎮守將軍、提督，各依品級給全葬，遣官讀文，致祭一次。

translations.literal: Inner grand ministers, commanders-in-chief, viscount-rank unattached grand ministers, grand secretaries, ministers, left censors, viscounts, hereditary viscounts, garrison generals, and provincial military commanders each received full burial by rank; an official read the eulogy and sacrificed once.
translations.idiomatic: Inner grand ministers, commanders-in-chief, viscount-rank grand ministers, grand secretaries, ministers, left censors, viscounts, hereditary viscounts, garrison generals, and provincial commanders received full burial by rank with one official sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 男品級散秩大臣、護軍統領、前鋒統領、副都統、侍郎、本身所得男、學士、副都御史、總督、總兵官、加級至二品巡撫，各依所加品級給全葬，遣官讀文，致祭一次。

translations.literal: Baron-rank unattached grand ministers, banner guard commanders, vanguard commanders, vice commanders-in-chief, vice ministers, personally received barons, academicians, vice censors, governors-general, regional commanders, and governors promoted to second rank each received full burial by added rank; an official read the eulogy and sacrificed once.
translations.idiomatic: Baron-rank grand ministers, banner guard, vanguard, and vice commanders, vice ministers, personally received barons, academicians, vice censors, governors-general, regional commanders, and governors promoted to second rank received full burial by added rank with one sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 三品侍郎、學士、副都御史、巡撫、通政使、大理寺卿，任滿給全葬，未滿者半之，俱遣官讀文，致祭一次。

translations.literal: Third-rank vice ministers, academicians, vice censors, governors, communications commissioners, and chief judges after full tenure received full burial; if not full, half; all had officials read eulogy and sacrifice once.
translations.idiomatic: Third-rank vice ministers, academicians, vice censors, governors, communications commissioners, and chief judges after full tenure received full burial; if not full, half; all one sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 布政使給全葬，致祭一次。

translations.literal: Provincial treasurers received full burial and sacrifice once.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial treasurers received full burial and one sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 雲騎尉、三等侍衛以上，文職知縣、武職守備以上陣亡者，各依加贈品級給全葬，致祭一次。

translations.literal: Cloud cavalry commanders, third-rank bodyguards and above, civil magistrates, and military garrison commanders and above killed in battle each received full burial by posthumously granted rank and sacrifice once.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud cavalry commanders, third-rank guards and above, magistrates, and garrison commanders killed in battle received full burial by posthumous rank and one sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 道光二十四年，定賜祭王、公以下儀，祭日，堂中陳儀衛，靈座前置供案，陳賜祭物品，左右分陳自備祭品。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang the ritual for bestowed sacrifice from prince and duke downward was fixed: on the sacrifice day guard of honor was displayed in the hall; before the spirit seat an offering table with bestowed sacrificial items; left and right with self-provided offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 24 ritual for bestowed sacrifice from prince downward was fixed: guard of honor in the hall, offering table before the spirit seat with bestowed items, self-provided offerings left and right.

sentences.zh: 案前設遣官奠位，東設祝案，北鄉，南設燎位，具楮帛。

translations.literal: Before the table the dispatched official's offering place was set; east an eulogy table facing north; south a burning place with spirit money and silks prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Before the table the dispatched official's place; east an eulogy table facing north; south a burning place with spirit money and silks.

sentences.zh: 遣官至，喪主率宗親及屬官跪迎大門外，禮部官奉祭文入自中門，陳東案，遣官隨入，就位立，喪主以下皆就位跪。

translations.literal: When the dispatched official arrived, the chief mourner led clan kin and subordinate officials to kneel and welcome outside the great gate; the rites official carried the sacrificial text in through the middle gate and placed it on the east table; the dispatched official entered and took position; the chief mourner and all took position and knelt.
translations.idiomatic: When the official arrived, the chief mourner led kin and subordinates to kneel and welcome at the great gate; the rites official carried the text through the middle gate to the east table; the official entered; all knelt in position.

sentences.zh: 讀祝官讀文訖，遣官跪奠三爵，每奠一叩。

translations.literal: When the eulogy reader finished, the dispatched official knelt and offered three libations, bowing once at each.
translations.idiomatic: When the eulogy reader finished, the official knelt and offered three libations, bowing once at each.

sentences.zh: 鎮國將軍以下立奠，喪主率眾隨行禮。

translations.literal: From banner commander of the state downward they stood to offer; the chief mourner led the assembly in following the rites.
translations.idiomatic: From banner commander downward they stood to offer; the chief mourner led the assembly in the rites.

sentences.zh: 畢，興，舉哀，燎祭文。

translations.literal: When complete they rose, wailed, and burned the sacrificial text.
translations.idiomatic: When complete they rose, wailed, and burned the text.

sentences.zh: 喪主率眾望闕謝恩，三跪九叩。

translations.literal: The chief mourner led the assembly to face the palace and give thanks, three kneelings and nine kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: The chief mourner led the assembly to face the palace in thanks, three kneelings and nine kowtows.

sentences.zh: 遣官出，跪送大門外。

translations.literal: The dispatched official departed; they knelt and escorted outside the great gate.
translations.idiomatic: The official departed; they knelt and escorted to the great gate.

sentences.zh: 賜諡親王例用一字，貝勒以下及文武大臣二字。

translations.literal: Posthumous titles for princes used one character by precedent; for beile and below and civil and military grand ministers, two characters.
translations.idiomatic: Princes' posthumous titles used one character; beile and below and civil and military ministers used two.

sentences.zh: 郡王諡號，尚沿明制用二字，間有用一字者。

translations.literal: Commandery-prince posthumous titles still followed Ming usage of two characters; occasionally one character was used.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery-prince titles still followed Ming two-character usage; occasionally one.

sentences.zh: 聖祖時，追諡郡王，滿、漢文俱用一字，遂為定制。

translations.literal: In the Sagely Ancestor's reign, when posthumously enfeoffing commandery princes, both Manchu and Chinese used one character, and this became regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi, posthumous commandery princes used one character in both Manchu and Chinese, and this became regulation.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，定親王以下喪聞，宗人府請諡，內院撰擬碑文。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi it was fixed that on report of death from prince of the blood downward, the Court of the Imperial Clan requested posthumous title and the inner court drafted the stele.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 9 on a prince's death the Court of the Imperial Clan requested a posthumous title and the inner court drafted the stele.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，定諸王賜諡，封號上加一字，貝勒以下、入八分公以上，予否請旨行。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi it was fixed that for princes granted posthumous titles, one character was added to the enfeoffment name; for beile and below and gong entered in the eight banners, grant or not was on imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 4 princes received one character added to the enfeoffment name; beile and gong in the eight banners required imperial order.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年，遵旨議定貝勒至輔國公兼一品職者予諡，仍請旨。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong, following imperial order it was deliberated and fixed that beile to auxiliary state duke also holding first-rank office might receive posthumous title, still requiring imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 36 beile to auxiliary state duke holding first-rank office might receive posthumous title, still by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 其兼二品以下職暨不兼職者罷予諡。

translations.literal: Those also holding second rank and below or holding no office were denied posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Those holding second rank and below or no office were denied posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 定制，一品官以上予否請上裁，二品官以下不獲請。

translations.literal: By regulation, for first-rank officials and above grant or not was at imperial discretion; second rank and below might not request.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation first-rank and above required imperial discretion; second rank and below could not request.

sentences.zh: 其得諡者，率出自特旨，或以勤勞，或以節義，或以文學，或以武功。

translations.literal: Those who received posthumous titles were mostly by special edict—for diligence, integrity, literary accomplishment, or military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Recipients were mostly by special edict—for diligence, integrity, letters, or arms.

sentences.zh: 破格崇褒，用示激勸。

translations.literal: Exceptional honors beyond precedent showed encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Exceptional honors beyond precedent encouraged merit.

sentences.zh: 嘉、道以前，諡典從嚴，往往有階至一品例可得而未得者。

translations.literal: Before Jiaqing and Daoguang the posthumous canon was strict; often those who had risen to first rank by precedent could have but did not.
translations.idiomatic: Before Jiaqing and Daoguang the canon was strict; many who qualified by first rank did not receive titles.

sentences.zh: 世宗朝，一等公福善，大學士魏裔介，將軍佛尼勒、莽依圖，都統馮國相，尚書湯斌、徐潮、瑪爾罕輩，望實素高，入祀賢良。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng reign, First-rank Duke Fushan, Grand Secretary Wei Yijie, Generals Foniye and Manggitu, Commander Feng Guoxiang, Ministers Tang Bin, Xu Chao, and Maerhan and others were of high repute and entered the shrine of worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng, Duke Fushan, Grand Secretary Wei Yijie, Generals Foniye and Manggitu, Commander Feng Guoxiang, Ministers Tang Bin, Xu Chao, Maerhan, and others of high repute entered the shrine of worthies.

sentences.zh: 逮至高宗初元，始獲追諡。

translations.literal: Only at the beginning of the Gaozong reign did they receive posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the beginning of Qianlong did they receive posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 易名盛典，殊不易得。

translations.literal: The great honor of changing the name was especially hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: The great honor of a posthumous name was especially hard to obtain.

sentences.zh: 令甲，得諡者禮部取旨，行知內閣典籍撰擬。

translations.literal: By regulation, those who received posthumous titles had the Ministry of Rites take imperial order and notify the Grand Secretariat archives to draft.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation the Ministry of Rites took imperial order and notified the Grand Secretariat archives to draft.

sentences.zh: 至穆宗朝，大學士卓秉恬改歸漢票簽，唯侍讀司之。

translations.literal: In the Muzong reign, Grand Secretary Zhuo Bingti changed this to Han ballot signing, handled only by the Reader's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Muzong, Grand Secretary Zhuo Bingti changed drafting to Han ballot signing by the Reader's Office.

sentences.zh: 大學士及翰林授職者，始得諡「文」，亦有出自特恩而獲諡文者。

translations.literal: Grand secretaries and Hanlin upon appointment might receive the character "Wen"; some received Wen by special grace.
translations.idiomatic: Grand secretaries and Hanlin upon appointment might receive "Wen"; some by special grace.

sentences.zh: 侍讀擬八字，大學士選四字，餘則擬十六字，大學士選八字，並請上裁定。

translations.literal: The reader drafted eight characters, the grand secretary chose four; others drafted sixteen, the grand secretary chose eight—all submitted for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: The reader drafted eight characters, the grand secretary chose four; others drafted sixteen, chose eight—all for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 武臣有諡文者，如領侍衛內大臣索尼獲諡文忠，異數也。

translations.literal: Military officials with Wen in the posthumous title, such as Inner Palace Guard Sonin receiving Wenzhong, were exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: Military officials with Wen, such as Sonin receiving Wenzhong, were exceptional.

sentences.zh: 唯「文正」則不敢擬，出自特恩。

translations.literal: Only "Wenzheng" was not drafted and came by special grace.
translations.idiomatic: Only "Wenzheng" was not drafted and came by special grace.

sentences.zh: 文職內自三品卿、外自布政使以下，例不予諡。

translations.literal: Civil officials from third-rank director inward and from provincial treasurer outward were not granted posthumous titles by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials from third-rank director inward and provincial treasurer outward were not granted titles by precedent.

sentences.zh: 唯御史陸隴其諡清獻，侍講學士秦承業諡文愨，太常卿唐鑒諡恪慎，則以崇尚儒臣，篤念師傅，不為恆式。

translations.literal: Only Censor Lu Longqi received Qingxian, Lecturer Qin Chengye Wenyue, and Chief of Ceremonies Tang Jian Kezhen—honoring Confucian ministers and honoring teachers, not constant precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Only Censor Lu Longqi Qingxian, Lecturer Qin Chengye Wenyue, and Chief of Ceremonies Tang Jian Kezhen—honoring Confucian ministers and teachers, not constant precedent.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，禮臣奏定文職二品官殉難，視一品予諡。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng the rites officials memorialized that civil officials of second rank who died for the state received posthumous title as first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 rites officials memorialized second-rank civil officials who died for the state received first-rank posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 如按察使優恤，禮部亦得援例以請。

translations.literal: As with surveillance commissioners receiving gracious condolence, the Ministry of Rites might cite precedent to request.
translations.idiomatic: As with surveillance commissioners receiving condolence, the Ministry of Rites might cite precedent.

sentences.zh: 軍興而後，道、府、州、縣等官死綏不少，疆臣疏請，不拘常格矣。

translations.literal: After military campaigns began, many circuit, prefectural, and county officials died holding their posts; frontier officials memorialized requests beyond constant precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After campaigns began, many local officials died in post; frontier officials requested beyond precedent.

sentences.zh: 其武職死事，參將以下，視副將議恤；

translations.literal: For military officials who died in service, from regimental commander downward condolence followed vice general;
translations.idiomatic: For military dead, from regimental commander downward condolence followed vice general;

sentences.zh: 協領以下，視副都統議恤：皆得援新章奏請。

translations.literal: from assistant commandant downward followed vice commander-in-chief: all might cite new regulations in memorial.
translations.idiomatic: from assistant commandant downward followed vice commander-in-chief: all might cite new regulations.

sentences.zh: 唯武功未成者，不得擬用「襄」字。

translations.literal: Only those without military achievement might not use the character Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Only those without military achievement might not use Xiang.

sentences.zh: 至十二年，諭：「嗣後文武各官，其官階例不予諡者，不得率行奏請。

translations.literal: By the twelfth year an edict ordered: "Hereafter for all civil and military officials whose rank by precedent does not receive posthumous title, memorial requests must not be made routinely."
translations.idiomatic: By the twelfth year an edict ordered: "Hereafter civil and military officials whose rank does not receive posthumous title by precedent must not routinely memorialize requests."

sentences.zh: 」至是限制稍嚴。

translations.literal: " From this the restrictions were somewhat stricter.
translations.idiomatic: From this the restrictions grew somewhat stricter.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，貴州巡撫黎培敬為已革總督賀長齡請諡。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu, Guizhou Governor Li Peijing requested a posthumous title for the dismissed Governor-General He Changling.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 4 Guizhou Governor Li Peijing requested a posthumous title for dismissed Governor-General He Changling.

sentences.zh: 詔以易名之典，不容冒濫，嚴切申儆，且下培敬吏議。

translations.literal: An edict said the honor of changing the name must not be abused; a stern warning was issued, and Li Peijing was referred for official censure.
translations.idiomatic: An edict held that posthumous honors must not be abused; a stern warning was issued and Li Peijing referred for censure.

sentences.zh: 亦有得諡而被奪者，若沈德潛、卞三元，或追論其生平，或敗露於身後，削秩仆碑，以示誡也。

translations.literal: There were also those who received posthumous titles but had them revoked, such as Shen Deqian and Bian Sanyuan—either their lives were rejudged or misconduct was exposed after death; rank was stripped and steles overturned to show warning.
translations.idiomatic: Some who received posthumous titles had them revoked, such as Shen Deqian and Bian Sanyuan—either rejudged in life or exposed after death; rank was stripped and steles overturned as warning.

sentences.zh: 至朝鮮國王諡號，曏亦內閣撰擬，嗣以所擬之字有觸其國王先代名諱，則改由其國自擬八字以進，請帝裁定雲。

translations.literal: As for posthumous titles of the king of Korea, formerly the inner court also drafted them; later because drafted characters sometimes tabooed former kings' names, Korea itself drafted eight characters for submission and the emperor decided.
translations.idiomatic: Korean kings' posthumous titles were formerly drafted by the inner court; later taboo conflicts led Korea to submit eight characters for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 外籓賜恤順治十三年，定蒙籓親王等喪，遣官★祭文至塋所宣讀致祭，喪主率屬跪迎。

translations.literal: Condolence in the outer domains: in the thirteenth year of Shunzhi it was fixed that when Mongol domain princes and the like died, an official was dispatched carrying sacrificial text to the burial place to proclaim and sacrifice; the chief mourner led dependents to kneel and welcome.
translations.idiomatic: Outer-domain condolence: in Shunzhi 13 when Mongol princes died, an official carried sacrificial text to the tomb to proclaim and sacrifice; the chief mourner led dependents to kneel and welcome.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，望闕謝恩，行三跪九拜禮。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete they faced the palace to give thanks, performing three kneelings and nine kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: When rites were complete they faced the palace in thanks with three kneelings and nine kowtows.

sentences.zh: 自王以下，致祭如前儀，唯牲醴物品，則依其爵為隆殺。

translations.literal: From king downward sacrifice followed the former ritual, only sacrificial livestock and offerings were graded by rank.
translations.idiomatic: From king downward sacrifice followed former ritual, with livestock and offerings graded by rank.

sentences.zh: 著有勛勞者，建碑優恤，特遣大臣、侍衛，出自恩旨。

translations.literal: Those with meritorious service received stele erection and gracious condolence; special dispatch of grand ministers and bodyguards came from imperial grace.
