translations.idiomatic: Those with merit received steles and gracious condolence; grand ministers and bodyguards were specially dispatched by grace.

sentences.zh: 親王、郡王福晉喪，遣祭如儀。

translations.literal: When a prince or commandery prince's consort died, sacrifice was dispatched as in the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When a prince or commandery prince's consort died, sacrifice was dispatched as in ritual.

sentences.zh: 貝勒至公夫人，並遣祭，無祭文。

translations.literal: From beile to gong's wives, sacrifice was also dispatched, without written eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: From beile to gong's wives sacrifice was dispatched without written eulogy.

sentences.zh: 其朝鮮國王母妃、王妃、世子喪訃至，禮臣請賜恤，遣正、副使賚祭品、香鈔諭祭。

translations.literal: When mourning news arrived for the queen mother, consorts, or heir of Korea, rites officials requested gracious condolence; chief and deputy envoys were sent with offerings and incense paper to proclaim sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning arrived for Korea's queen mother, consorts, or heir, rites officials requested condolence; chief and deputy envoys bore offerings and incense paper to sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十一年，國王世子李氄喪，禮部奏聞。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of Qianlong the heir of the kingdom, Li Rou, died; the Ministry of Rites memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 51 the Korean heir Li Rou died; the Ministry of Rites memorialized.

sentences.zh: 詔以朝鮮世守籓封，最稱恭順，命倍給祭品，示優恤。

translations.literal: An edict said Korea had long guarded the domain border with utmost deference; orders were given to double the offerings to show gracious condolence.
translations.idiomatic: An edict noted Korea's long faithful guarding of the border; offerings were doubled to show gracious condolence.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年，國王李鍚曾祖母庄順王妃訃至，賜祭一次。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiaqing mourning news arrived for King Li Xi's great-grandmother, Consort Zhuangshun; sacrifice was granted once.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 10 mourning arrived for King Li Xi's great-grandmother Consort Zhuangshun; one sacrifice was granted.

sentences.zh: 琉球、越南國王卒，告哀，遣使諭祭，並給銀絹。

translations.literal: When kings of Ryukyu and Vietnam died they reported grief; envoys were dispatched to proclaim sacrifice and silver and silk were granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Ryukyu and Vietnamese kings died they reported grief; envoys proclaimed sacrifice and silver and silk were granted.

sentences.zh: 母、妃、世子喪，俱不告哀，不賜恤。

translations.literal: For death of mother, consort, or heir they did not report grief and no condolence was granted.
translations.idiomatic: For mother, consort, or heir they did not report grief and received no condolence.

sentences.zh: 使臣來京病歿，則題請恤典，賜棺及祭，歸葬者聽。

translations.literal: If envoys died ill in the capital, condolence was memorialized; coffin and sacrifice were granted, and return for burial was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys who died ill in the capital received memorialized condolence, coffin and sacrifice, and might return for burial.

sentences.zh: 品官喪禮定制，有疾遷正寢，疾革書遺言，三品以上官具遺疏，既終乃哭。

translations.literal: Mourning rites for ranked officials: by regulation, when ill one moved to the main chamber; when critically ill one wrote final instructions; officials of third rank and above prepared a final memorial; when life ended then came weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Ranked officials' mourning: by regulation the ill moved to the main chamber; the dying wrote final instructions; third rank and above prepared a final memorial; weeping began at death.

sentences.zh: 立喪主、主婦。

translations.literal: A chief mourner and mistress of mourning were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: A chief mourner and mistress of mourning were appointed.

sentences.zh: 護喪諸執事人治棺，民公采板，侯、伯、一品官以下硃棺。

translations.literal: Funeral stewards prepared the coffin: civilian dukes used selected planks; marquises, earls, and first-rank officials downward used vermilion coffins.
translations.idiomatic: Stewards prepared the coffin: civilian dukes used selected planks; marquises, earls, and first rank downward used vermilion coffins.

sentences.zh: 訃告。

translations.literal: Death notice was sent.
translations.idiomatic: Death notice was sent.

sentences.zh: 設屍床、帷堂，陳沐具。

translations.literal: A corpse bed and mourning hall were set up, bathing implements displayed.
translations.idiomatic: A corpse bed and mourning hall were set up with bathing implements.

sentences.zh: 乃含。

translations.literal: Then mouth-placing.
translations.idiomatic: Then mouth-placing.

sentences.zh: 三品以上用小珠玉，七品以上用金木屑五。

translations.literal: Third rank and above used small pearls and jade; seventh rank and above used gold filings, five measures.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above used small pearls and jade; seventh rank and above used five measures of gold filings.

sentences.zh: 襲衣，常服一稱，朝衣冠帶各以其等。

translations.literal: Dressing garments: one set of ordinary dress; court dress, hat, robe, and belt each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Dressing garments: one ordinary set; court dress, hat, robe, and belt by rank.

sentences.zh: 明日小斂，陳斂床堂東，加斂衣，三品以上五稱，複三、襌二；

translations.literal: The next day minor encoffining: an encoffining bed east of the hall, additional garments—fifth rank and above five sets, three lined and two unlined;
translations.idiomatic: Next day minor encoffining: encoffining bed east of the hall, additional garments—third rank and above five sets, three lined and two unlined;

sentences.zh: 五品以上三稱，複二、襌一；

translations.literal: fifth rank and above three sets, two lined and one unlined;
translations.idiomatic: fifth rank and above three sets, two lined and one unlined;

sentences.zh: 六品以下二稱，複、襌各一：皆以繒。

translations.literal: sixth rank and below two sets, one lined and one unlined—all of silk.
translations.idiomatic: sixth rank and below two sets, one lined and one unlined—all silk.

sentences.zh: 複衾一。

translations.literal: One lined coverlet.
translations.idiomatic: One lined coverlet.

sentences.zh: 又明日大斂蓋棺，設靈床柩東，柩前設靈座，陳奠幾，喪主及諸子居苫次，族人各服其服。

translations.literal: The next day major encoffining and coffin closed; a spirit bed east of the coffin, spirit seat before the coffin, offering table set out; the chief mourner and sons dwelt in the mourning hut; clan members each wore their mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Next day major encoffining and lid closed; spirit bed east of coffin, spirit seat before it, offering table; chief mourner and sons in the mourning hut; clan in mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 朝夕奠肴饌，午餅餌。

translations.literal: Morning and evening offerings of meat dishes; at noon cakes and pastries.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening meat offerings; at noon cakes and pastries.

sentences.zh: 遇朔望，則朝奠具殷奠，餚核加盛。

translations.literal: On new and full moon, morning offering with full offerings; dishes and fruits more abundant.
translations.idiomatic: On new and full moon, morning offering with fuller dishes and fruits.

sentences.zh: 初祭，陳饌筵羊酒，具楮幣。

translations.literal: At first sacrifice, food tables, sheep, and wine were displayed with spirit money.
translations.idiomatic: First sacrifice displayed food tables, sheep, wine, and spirit money.

sentences.zh: 公筵十五席，羊七，楮四萬；

translations.literal: Duke's table fifteen settings, seven sheep, forty thousand sheets of spirit money;
translations.idiomatic: Duke: fifteen tables, seven sheep, forty thousand sheets;

sentences.zh: 侯筵十二，楮三萬六千；

translations.literal: marquis twelve tables, thirty-six thousand sheets;
translations.idiomatic: marquis: twelve tables, thirty-six thousand sheets;

sentences.zh: 伯筵十二，楮三萬二千：羊俱六。

translations.literal: earl twelve tables, thirty-two thousand sheets; six sheep each.
translations.idiomatic: earl: twelve tables, thirty-two thousand sheets; six sheep each.

sentences.zh: 一品官筵十，羊五，楮二萬八千；

translations.literal: First-rank official ten tables, five sheep, twenty-eight thousand sheets;
translations.idiomatic: First rank: ten tables, five sheep, twenty-eight thousand sheets;

sentences.zh: 二品筵八，羊四，楮二萬四千；

translations.literal: second rank eight tables, four sheep, twenty-four thousand sheets;
translations.idiomatic: second rank: eight tables, four sheep, twenty-four thousand sheets;

sentences.zh: 三品筵六，楮二萬；

translations.literal: third rank six tables, twenty thousand sheets;
translations.idiomatic: third rank: six tables, twenty thousand sheets;

sentences.zh: 四品筵五，楮萬六千：羊俱三。

translations.literal: fourth rank five tables, sixteen thousand sheets; three sheep each.
translations.idiomatic: fourth rank: five tables, sixteen thousand sheets; three sheep each.

sentences.zh: 五品筵四，楮萬二千；

translations.literal: Fifth rank four tables, twelve thousand sheets;
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank: four tables, twelve thousand sheets;

sentences.zh: 六、七品筵三，楮萬：羊俱二。

translations.literal: sixth and seventh rank three tables, ten thousand sheets; two sheep each.
translations.idiomatic: sixth and seventh rank: three tables, ten thousand sheets; two sheep each.

sentences.zh: 族人齊集，喪主以下再拜，哭奠如禮。

translations.literal: Clan members assembled; the chief mourner and below bowed twice and wailed and offered according to rite.
translations.idiomatic: Clan assembled; chief mourner and below bowed twice, wailed, and offered by rite.

sentences.zh: 卒奠，大功者易素服，大祭同。

translations.literal: When offering was complete, those in nine-month mourning changed to plain dress; the great sacrifice was the same.
translations.idiomatic: When offering ended, nine-month mourners changed to plain dress; great sacrifice likewise.

sentences.zh: 初祭，期服者易素服，百日致奠薙髮，三月而葬。

translations.literal: At first sacrifice those in one-year mourning changed to plain dress; at the hundredth day offering hair was cut; burial in the third month.
translations.idiomatic: At first sacrifice one-year mourners changed to plain dress; hundredth-day offering cut hair; burial in the third month.

sentences.zh: 一品塋地九十步，封丈有六尺，遞殺至二十步封二尺止。

translations.literal: First rank: grave plot ninety paces, mound one zhang six chi, decreasing to twenty paces and mound two chi.
translations.idiomatic: First rank: grave ninety paces, mound one zhang six chi, decreasing to twenty paces and two chi.

sentences.zh: 繚以垣。

translations.literal: Surrounded by a wall.
translations.idiomatic: Surrounded by a wall.

sentences.zh: 公、侯、伯周四十丈，守塋四戶；

translations.literal: Dukes, marquises, and earls: perimeter forty zhang, four tomb-guard households;
translations.idiomatic: Dukes, marquises, earls: forty-zhang perimeter, four tomb-guard households;

sentences.zh: 二品以上周三十五丈，二戶；

translations.literal: second rank and above thirty-five zhang, two households;
translations.idiomatic: second rank and above: thirty-five zhang, two households;

sentences.zh: 五品以上周三十丈，一戶；

translations.literal: fifth rank and above thirty zhang, one household;
translations.idiomatic: fifth rank and above: thirty zhang, one household;

sentences.zh: 六品以下周十二丈，止二人守之。

translations.literal: sixth rank and below twelve zhang, only two guards.
translations.idiomatic: sixth rank and below: twelve zhang, two guards only.

sentences.zh: 公至二品，用石人、望柱暨虎、羊、馬各二，三品無石人，四品無石羊，五品無石虎。

translations.literal: From duke to second rank, stone figures, pillar stones, and tigers, sheep, and horses two each; third rank no stone figures; fourth rank no stone sheep; fifth rank no stone tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Duke to second rank: stone figures, pillars, tigers, sheep, and horses two each; third rank no figures; fourth no sheep; fifth no tigers.

sentences.zh: 其墓門勒碑，公、侯、伯螭首高三尺二寸，碑身高九尺，廣三尺六寸，龜趺高三尺八寸。

translations.literal: Tomb gate stele: duke, marquis, earl dragon head three chi two cun high, stele body nine chi, width three chi six cun, tortoise base three chi eight cun.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb stele: duke, marquis, earl dragon head three chi two cun, body nine chi by three chi six cun, tortoise base three chi eight cun.

sentences.zh: 一品螭首，二品麒麟首，三品天祿辟邪首。

translations.literal: First rank dragon head; second rank qilin head; third rank tianlu and piexie heads.
translations.idiomatic: First rank dragon head; second qilin; third tianlu and piexie.

sentences.zh: 四至七品圓首方趺，首視公、侯、伯遞殺二尺至尺八寸止，碑身遞殺五寸至五尺五寸止，廣遞殺二寸至二尺二寸止，趺遞殺二寸至二尺四寸止。

translations.literal: Fourth to seventh rank round head and square base; head decreasing two chi to one chi eight cun from duke precedent; stele body five cun to five chi five cun; width two cun to two chi two cun; base two cun to two chi four cun.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth to seventh round head and square base, dimensions decreasing stepwise from ducal precedent.

sentences.zh: 刻壙志用石二片，一為蓋，書某官之墓，一為底，書姓名、鄉里、三代、生年、卒葬月日及子孫葬地。

translations.literal: Burial record carved on two stone slabs, one lid inscribed with office and tomb, one base with name, native place, three generations, birth and death and burial dates, and descendants' burial ground.
translations.idiomatic: Burial record on two stones: lid with office and tomb, base with name, place, three generations, dates, and descendants' ground.

sentences.zh: 婦人則隨夫與子孫封贈。

translations.literal: For women it followed husband and sons' enfeoffment and grants.
translations.idiomatic: For women it followed husband and sons' titles.

sentences.zh: 二石相鄉，鐵束，埋墓中。

translations.literal: The two stones faced each other, bound with iron, buried in the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The two stones faced each other, iron-bound, buried in the tomb.

sentences.zh: 制柩轝，上用竹格，結以采，旁施帷幔，四角垂流蘇，繒荒、繒幃並青藍色。

translations.literal: Funeral carriage made: upper frame of bamboo latticed and colored, side curtains, tassels at four corners, silk cover and silk canopy all blue.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral carriage: bamboo frame colored, side curtains, corner tassels, blue silk cover and canopy.

sentences.zh: 公、侯、伯織五采，一、二品用銷金，五品以上畫雲氣，六、七品素繒無飾。

translations.literal: Dukes, marquises, earls wove five colors; first and second rank used gilt; fifth rank and above painted cloud patterns; sixth and seventh plain silk without ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes wove five colors; first and second rank gilt; fifth rank and above cloud patterns; sixth and seventh plain silk.

sentences.zh: 承以槓，五品以上魨硃，六、七品飾紅堊，障柩畫翣，五品以上四，六、七品二。

translations.literal: Borne on poles; fifth rank and above poles lacquered vermilion, sixth and seventh red clay; screen painted fans—four for fifth rank and above, two for sixth and seventh.
translations.idiomatic: Poles: fifth rank and above lacquered vermilion, sixth and seventh red clay; screen fans four or two by rank.

sentences.zh: 引布二，功布一，靈車一，明器則從俗。

translations.literal: Two guide cloths, one merit cloth, one spirit carriage; grave goods followed custom.
translations.idiomatic: Two guide cloths, one merit cloth, one spirit carriage; grave goods by custom.

sentences.zh: 諏日發引，前夕祖奠，翌日遣奠，會葬者畢集。

translations.literal: On the chosen day the procession set out; the eve before, offering to the road; next day farewell offering; all who joined the burial assembled.
translations.idiomatic: On the chosen day the procession set out; eve offering to the road; next day farewell; all mourners assembled.

sentences.zh: 公鞍馬八，遞殺至二數。

translations.literal: Duke eight saddle horses, decreasing to two.
translations.idiomatic: Duke eight saddle horses, decreasing to two.

sentences.zh: 儀從前導，引以丹旐、銘旌，滿用丹旐，漢用銘旌。

translations.literal: Escort led the way; red banners and epitaph banners led—Manchu used red banners, Han used epitaph banners.
translations.idiomatic: Escort led; red and epitaph banners—Manchu red, Han epitaph.

sentences.zh: 至墓所，乃窆。

translations.literal: At the grave they buried.
translations.idiomatic: At the grave they buried.

sentences.zh: 祀后土，題主，奉安，升車，反哭，乃虞。

translations.literal: Sacrificed to the earth god, inscribed the tablet, enshrined, mounted the carriage, returned to wail, then yu offering.
translations.idiomatic: They sacrificed to the earth god, inscribed the tablet, enshrined, mounted the carriage, returned to wail, then yu offering.

sentences.zh: 羊、酒、楮帛各視其等。

translations.literal: Sheep, wine, and silks each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep, wine, and silks by rank.

sentences.zh: 祭畢，柔日再虞，剛日三虞。

translations.literal: When sacrifice was complete, on a soft day second yu, on a firm day third yu.
translations.idiomatic: After sacrifice, second yu on a soft day, third yu on a firm day.

sentences.zh: 百日卒哭，次日祔家廟。

translations.literal: At the hundredth day final wailing ended; next day enshrined in the family temple.
translations.idiomatic: Hundredth day ended wailing; next day enshrined in the family temple.

sentences.zh: 期年小祥，再期大祥，遷主入廟。

translations.literal: At one year lesser felicity, at two years greater felicity, the tablet moved into the temple.
translations.idiomatic: One year lesser felicity, two years greater felicity, tablet moved to the temple.

sentences.zh: 祝讀告辭，主人俯伏五拜。

translations.literal: The invoker read the announcement; the master prostrated himself five times.
translations.idiomatic: The invoker read the announcement; the master prostrated five times.

sentences.zh: 訖，改題神主，詣廟設東室，奉祧主藏夾室。

translations.literal: When done the spirit tablet was retitled; they went to the temple to set the eastern chamber and stored the distant ancestor tablet in the side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Then the tablet was retitled; eastern chamber set and distant ancestor stored in the side chamber.

sentences.zh: 乃徹靈座。

translations.literal: Then the spirit seat was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Then the spirit seat was removed.

sentences.zh: 後一月禫。

translations.literal: One month later the dan rite.
translations.idiomatic: One month later the dan rite.

sentences.zh: 喪至此計二十有七月。

translations.literal: Mourning to this point totaled twenty-seven months.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning totaled twenty-seven months.

sentences.zh: 喪主詣廟祗薦禫事。

translations.literal: The chief mourner went to the temple to reverently offer the dan rite.
translations.idiomatic: The chief mourner offered the dan rite at the temple.

sentences.zh: 其在外聞喪者，訃至，易服，哭，奔喪。

translations.literal: Those who heard of mourning while away: when notice arrived they changed dress, wept, and hurried home for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Those abroad on news of death changed dress, wept, and hurried home.

sentences.zh: 至家憑殯哭，翌日成服。

translations.literal: Arriving home they wept before the coffin; next day they donned mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: At home they wept before the coffin; next day they donned mourning.

sentences.zh: 喪期自聞訃日始。

translations.literal: The mourning period began from the day notice was received.
translations.idiomatic: The mourning period began from the day notice arrived.

sentences.zh: 餘同。

translations.literal: The rest was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The rest was the same.

sentences.zh: 期以下聞喪，易服為位而哭，奔喪，則至家成服。

translations.literal: For mourning below one-year grade on hearing news, they changed dress, set a place and wept, hurried home, and at arrival donned mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Below one-year grade: change dress, weep in place, hurry home, don mourning on arrival.

sentences.zh: 官在職，非本生父母喪，雖期，猶從政，不奔喪。

translations.literal: Officials in office, for mourning other than birth parents even at one-year grade, still attended to duties and did not hurry home.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in office, except for birth parents even at one-year grade, attended duties and did not hurry home.

sentences.zh: 聞訃，易服為位而哭，私居持服，入公門治事仍常服。

translations.literal: On hearing notice they changed dress, set a place and wept, wore mourning in private, but in public gates still wore ordinary dress for business.
translations.idiomatic: On notice they changed dress and wept in private, but wore ordinary dress in public for business.

sentences.zh: 期喪者，期年不與朝、祭。

translations.literal: Those in one-year mourning did not attend court or sacrifices for one year.
translations.idiomatic: One-year mourners did not attend court or sacrifices for one year.

sentences.zh: 服滿，則於私居為位哭，除之。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete, at home they set a place and wept, then laid it aside.
translations.idiomatic: When complete, at home they wept at a set place and laid mourning aside.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，定百官親喪祭禮以其子品級，子視父母，命婦視夫同。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi it was fixed that sacrifice at parents' mourning for the hundred officials followed their sons' rank; sons followed parents, titled ladies followed husbands likewise.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 9 parents' mourning sacrifices for officials followed sons' rank; sons and titled ladies followed parents and husbands.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十六年，禁居喪演戲飲博。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Kangxi, performing plays, gambling, and drinking during mourning residence was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 26 plays, gambling, and drinking in mourning residence were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 凡官卒任所，或父母與妻喪，許入城治事。

translations.literal: Whenever an official died in his post, or parents or wife died, entry to the city to conduct business was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When an official died in post, or parents or wife died, entry to the city for business was permitted.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，諭京旗文武官遇親喪，百日後即入署治事，持服如故。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong reign an edict ordered capital banner civil and military officials on parents' mourning to enter office after a hundred days while still wearing mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong, capital banner officials on parents' mourning entered office after a hundred days while still in mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 罷與祭祀、朝會。

translations.literal: Participation in sacrifices and court assemblies was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices and court assemblies were discontinued.

sentences.zh: 道光二十四年，定民公以下、軍民以上居喪二十七月，不宴會、作樂，不娶妻、納妾，門戶不換舊符。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang it was fixed that from civilian duke downward and soldiers and civilians upward, mourning residence twenty-seven months, no banquets or music, no marriage or taking concubines, door talismans not changed.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 24 civilian dukes down and soldiers and civilians up mourned twenty-seven months without banquets, music, marriage, or concubines; door talismans unchanged.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，禮部議畫一滿、漢喪制，自是滿官親喪去職，與漢官一例矣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong the Ministry of Rites deliberated unifying Manchu and Han mourning systems; thereafter Manchu officials left office on parents' mourning like Han officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1 the Ministry of Rites unified Manchu and Han mourning; thereafter Manchu officials left office on parents' mourning like Han.

sentences.zh: 士庶人喪禮順治初年，定制，士、庶卒，用硃棺，櫬一層，鞍馬一。

translations.literal: Mourning rites for gentry and commoners: in early Shunzhi regulation was fixed: when gentry or commoners died, vermilion coffins with one layer of padding, one saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners: early Shunzhi regulation used vermilion coffins with one padding layer and one saddle horse.

sentences.zh: 初祭用引幡，金銀楮幣各一千，祭筵三，羊一。

translations.literal: First sacrifice used a funeral banner, a thousand sheets each of gold and silver spirit money, three offering tables, one sheep.
translations.idiomatic: First sacrifice: one banner, a thousand gold and silver spirit sheets each, three tables, one sheep.

sentences.zh: 大祭同。

translations.literal: Great sacrifice was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Great sacrifice was the same.

sentences.zh: 百日、期年祭，視初祭半之。

translations.literal: Hundredth-day and anniversary sacrifices were half the first sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Hundredth-day and anniversary sacrifices were half the first.

sentences.zh: 一月殯，三月葬。

translations.literal: Encoffining in one month, burial in three months.
translations.idiomatic: Encoffining in one month, burial in three.

sentences.zh: 墓祭紙幣、酒肴有定數。

translations.literal: Tomb sacrifice paper money and wine and dishes had fixed amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb sacrifice paper money, wine, and dishes had fixed amounts.

sentences.zh: 通禮，士斂衣複襌各一，複衾一，襲常服一稱，含用金銀屑三，用銘旌。

translations.literal: By the Comprehensive Rites, for gentry encoffining garments one lined and one unlined each, one lined coverlet, one set of ordinary dress for dressing, mouth-placing used three measures of gold and silver filings, epitaph banner used.
translations.idiomatic: By the Comprehensive Rites, gentry used one lined and one unlined garment, one lined coverlet, one ordinary dressing set, three measures of gold and silver filings for mouth-placing, and an epitaph banner.

sentences.zh: 庶人複衾一，含銀屑三，立魂帛。

translations.literal: Commoners one lined coverlet, mouth-placing three measures of silver filings, spirit cloth erected.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners used one lined coverlet, three measures of silver filings for mouth-placing, and a spirit cloth.

sentences.zh: 士塋地圍二十步，封高六尺。

translations.literal: Gentry grave plot perimeter twenty paces, mound six chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry graves: twenty-pace perimeter, six-chi mound.

sentences.zh: 墓門石碣，圓首方趺。

translations.literal: Tomb gate stone tablet, round head and square base.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb gate stone tablet with round head and square base.

sentences.zh: 壙志二，如官儀。

translations.literal: Two burial records, as for officials.
translations.idiomatic: Two burial records, as for officials.

sentences.zh: 柩轝上竹格垂流蘇，槓飾紅堊，無翣。

translations.literal: Funeral carriage upper bamboo frame with hanging tassels, poles decorated red clay, no screen fans.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral carriage: bamboo frame with tassels, poles in red clay, no screen fans.

sentences.zh: 引布二，功布一。

translations.literal: Two guide cloths, one merit cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Two guide cloths, one merit cloth.

sentences.zh: 靈車一。

translations.literal: One spirit carriage.
translations.idiomatic: One spirit carriage.

sentences.zh: 明器從俗。

translations.literal: Grave goods followed custom.
translations.idiomatic: Grave goods followed custom.

sentences.zh: 庶人塋地九步，封四尺。

translations.literal: Commoners grave plot nine paces, mound four chi.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners: nine-pace plot, four-chi mound.

sentences.zh: 有志無碣。

translations.literal: Burial record but no stele.
translations.idiomatic: Burial record but no stele.

sentences.zh: 轝以布衾覆棺，不施幃蓋。

translations.literal: Carriage covered the coffin with cloth quilt, no canopy or cover hung.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage covered the coffin with a cloth quilt, without canopy or cover.

sentences.zh: 槓兩端飾黑，中飾紅堊。

translations.literal: Pole ends decorated black, middle decorated red clay.
translations.idiomatic: Pole ends black, middle red clay.

sentences.zh: 餘略仿品官，制從殺。

translations.literal: The rest roughly followed ranked officials, regulations reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The rest roughly followed officials at reduced scale.

sentences.zh: 雍正初元，定軍、民故者，前後斂衣五襲，鞍馬一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng it was fixed for deceased soldiers and civilians: five sets of encoffining garments before and after, one saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 deceased soldiers and civilians received five encoffining sets and one saddle horse.

sentences.zh: 初祭，祭筵二，羊一，大祭同，常祭減半。

translations.literal: First sacrifice two offering tables, one sheep; great sacrifice the same; regular sacrifices halved.
translations.idiomatic: First sacrifice: two tables, one sheep; great sacrifice the same; regular sacrifices halved.

sentences.zh: 棺罩生、監用青絹，軍、民春布。

translations.literal: Coffin canopy for licentiates and students used blue silk; soldiers and civilians spring cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Licentiates and students used blue silk coffin canopies; soldiers and civilians spring cloth.

sentences.zh: 十三年，詔曰：「朕聞外省百姓喪葬侈靡，甚至招集親鄰，開筵劇飲，名曰鬧喪，且於喪所殯時雜陳百戲。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year an edict said: "We have heard that in the provinces common people's funerals are extravagant, even gathering kin and neighbors to open feasts and drink heavily, called 'rowdy mourning,' and at the mourning place during encoffining they mix in a hundred entertainments."
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year an edict said: "We hear provincial funerals are extravagant, with kin gathered for feasts and heavy drinking called 'rowdy mourning,' and entertainments mixed in at the mourning place."

sentences.zh: 匪唯背理，抑亦忍情。

translations.literal: "This is not only contrary to reason but also cruel to feeling."
translations.idiomatic: "This is not only contrary to reason but cruel to feeling."

sentences.zh: 」敕督撫嚴禁陋習，違者治罪。

translations.literal: " Governors-general and governors were ordered strictly to forbid vulgar customs; violators were punished."
translations.idiomatic: Governors-general and governors were ordered to forbid vulgar customs; violators were punished.

sentences.zh: 又諭：「吉凶異道，不得相干。

translations.literal: An edict also said: "Auspicious and inauspicious ways must not interfere."
translations.idiomatic: An edict also said: "Auspicious and inauspicious rites must not interfere."

sentences.zh: 故娶在三年外而聘在三年內者，春秋猶以為非。

translations.literal: "Thus marriage after three years while betrothal within three years—the Spring and Autumn Annals still regarded it as wrong."
translations.idiomatic: "Thus marrying after three years while betrothed within three years—the Spring and Autumn Annals still judged it wrong."

sentences.zh: 三年之喪，創深痛鉅。

translations.literal: "Three-year mourning wounds are deep and pain immense."
translations.idiomatic: "Three-year mourning wounds are deep and pain immense."

sentences.zh: 乃愚民不知禮教，慮服喪後不獲嫁娶，遂乘父母疾篤或殯斂未終而貿然為之者，朕甚憫焉。

translations.literal: "Yet foolish people ignorant of ritual teaching, fearing they could not marry after mourning, rashly did so while parents were critically ill or before encoffining ended—We pity them greatly."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet the ignorant, fearing no marriage after mourning, rashly married while parents were dying or before encoffining ended—We pity them greatly."

sentences.zh: 自今伊始，齒朝之士，下逮生監，毋違此制。

translations.literal: "From now on, court officials down to licentiates and students must not violate this regulation."
translations.idiomatic: "From now on, court officials down to licentiates and students must not violate this."

sentences.zh: 其皁隸編氓，窮而無告，父母臥疾，賴子婦治饔飧者，任其迎娶盥饋，俟疾瘳或服竟再成婚禮。

translations.literal: "For black-robed commoners poor and helpless, when parents lay ill relying on sons and daughters-in-law for meals, they may receive marriage and serve food and drink, then complete the marriage rite after recovery or when mourning ends."
translations.idiomatic: "For poor commoners whose ill parents rely on sons and daughters-in-law for meals, preliminary marriage and serving food are permitted, with full marriage after recovery or mourning ends."

sentences.zh: 」古者禮不下庶人，其斯之謂歟？

translations.literal: " In antiquity ritual did not descend to commoners—is this not what is meant?"
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity ritual did not descend to commoners—is this not what is meant?

sentences.zh: 曾子問：「親迎在途而婿之父母死，女改服布深衣、縞總以趨喪。

translations.literal: Zengzi asked: "If while going to receive the bride the bridegroom's parents die, the woman changes to deep hemp garment and white headband to hurry to mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Zengzi asked: "If the bridegroom's parents die while he is fetching the bride, the woman changes to deep hemp and white headband to hurry to mourning."

sentences.zh: 」亦此義也。

translations.literal: " This too is the meaning."
translations.idiomatic: This too is the meaning.

sentences.zh: 服制順治三年，定喪服制，列圖於律，頒行中外。

translations.literal: Mourning dress regulations: in the third year of Shunzhi mourning dress was fixed, charts entered in the code, and promulgated within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning dress: in Shunzhi 3 regulations were fixed, charts entered in the code, and promulgated everywhere.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，增輯大清通禮，所載冠、服、絰、屨，多沿前代舊制。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang the Comprehensive Rites of the Great Qing was enlarged; caps, garments, headbands, and shoes mostly followed former dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 4 the Comprehensive Rites of the Great Qing was enlarged; caps, garments, bands, and shoes mostly followed former dynasties.

sentences.zh: 制服五：曰斬衰服，生麻布，旁及下際不緝。

translations.literal: Five garment types: first, zhan mourning garment—raw hemp cloth, edges and lower hem unhemmed.
translations.idiomatic: Five garment types: zhan mourning—raw hemp, edges and lower hem unhemmed.

sentences.zh: 麻冠、絰，菅屨，竹杖。

translations.literal: Hemp cap and headband, rush shoes, bamboo staff.
translations.idiomatic: Hemp cap and band, rush shoes, bamboo staff.

sentences.zh: 婦人麻屨，不杖。

translations.literal: Women hemp shoes, no staff.
translations.idiomatic: Women hemp shoes, no staff.

sentences.zh: 曰齊衰服，熟麻布，旁及下際緝，麻冠、絰，草屨，桐杖。

translations.literal: Second, qi mourning garment—processed hemp, edges and lower hem hemmed, hemp cap and headband, straw shoes, paulownia staff.
translations.idiomatic: Second, qi mourning—processed hemp, hemmed edges, hemp cap and band, straw shoes, paulownia staff.

sentences.zh: 婦人仍麻屨。

translations.literal: Women still hemp shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Women still hemp shoes.

sentences.zh: 曰大功服，粗白布，冠、絰如之，繭布緣屨。

translations.literal: Third, da gong garment—coarse white cloth, cap and headband likewise, silk-edged shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Third, da gong—coarse white cloth, matching cap and band, silk-edged shoes.

sentences.zh: 曰小功服，稍細白布，冠、屨如前。

translations.literal: Fourth, xiao gong garment—somewhat finer white cloth, cap and shoes as before.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, xiao gong—finer white cloth, cap and shoes as before.

sentences.zh: 曰緦麻服，細白布，絰帶同，素屨無飾。

translations.literal: Fifth, si hemp garment—fine white cloth, headband likewise, plain unadorned shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, si hemp—fine white cloth, matching band, plain shoes.

sentences.zh: 敘服八：曰斬衰三年，子為父、母；

translations.literal: Eight graded garments: first, zhan three years—son for father and mother;
translations.idiomatic: Eight graded garments: zhan three years—son for father and mother;

sentences.zh: 為繼母、慈母、養母、嫡母、生母；

translations.literal: for stepmother, nurturing mother, adoptive mother, principal mother, birth mother;
translations.idiomatic: for stepmother, nurturing mother, adoptive mother, principal mother, birth mother;

sentences.zh: 為人後者為所後父、母；

translations.literal: for one who becomes heir, for adoptive father and mother;
translations.idiomatic: for an heir, for adoptive father and mother;

sentences.zh: 子之妻同。

translations.literal: son's wife likewise.
translations.idiomatic: son's wife likewise.

sentences.zh: 女在室為父、母及已嫁被出而反者同；

translations.literal: Daughter unmarried for father and mother, and one married but expelled and returned likewise;
translations.idiomatic: Unmarried daughter for father and mother, and married but expelled and returned likewise;

sentences.zh: 嫡孫為祖父、母或高、曾祖父、母承重；

translations.literal: Principal grandson for grandfather and grandmother, or great-grandfather and great-grandmother bearing the main line;
translations.idiomatic: Principal grandson for grandparents or great-grandparents bearing the main line;

sentences.zh: 妻為夫，妾為家長同。

translations.literal: Wife for husband, concubine for householder likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Wife for husband, concubine for householder likewise.

sentences.zh: 曰齊衰杖期，嫡子、眾子為庶母；

translations.literal: Second, qi with staff one-year term—principal son and all sons for concubine mother;
translations.idiomatic: Second, qi with staff one year—principal and all sons for concubine mother;

sentences.zh: 子之妻同；

translations.literal: son's wife likewise;
translations.idiomatic: son's wife likewise;

sentences.zh: 子為嫁母、出母；

translations.literal: son for remarried mother or expelled mother;
translations.idiomatic: son for remarried or expelled mother;

sentences.zh: 夫為妻；

translations.literal: husband for wife;
translations.idiomatic: husband for wife;

sentences.zh: 嫡孫祖在為祖母承重。

translations.literal: principal grandson while grandfather lives bears grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: principal grandson while grandfather lives bears grandmother.

sentences.zh: 曰齊衰不杖期，為伯、叔父、母；

translations.literal: Third, qi without staff one-year term—for paternal uncle and aunt;
translations.idiomatic: Third, qi without staff one year—for paternal uncle and aunt;

sentences.zh: 為親兄、弟；

translations.literal: for full elder and younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: for full elder and younger brother;

sentences.zh: 為親兄、弟之子及女在室者；

translations.literal: for full elder and younger brother's son and unmarried daughter;
translations.idiomatic: for full brother's son and unmarried daughter;

sentences.zh: 為同居繼父兩無大功以上親者；

translations.literal: for stepfather cohabiting with neither having da gong kin or closer;
translations.idiomatic: for cohabiting stepfather with neither side having da gong kin or closer;

sentences.zh: 祖為嫡孫；

translations.literal: grandfather for principal grandson;
translations.idiomatic: grandfather for principal grandson;

sentences.zh: 父、母為鏑長子及眾子；

translations.literal: father and mother for eldest son and all sons;
translations.idiomatic: father and mother for eldest son and all sons;

sentences.zh: 為嫡長子妻；

translations.literal: for principal eldest son's wife;
translations.idiomatic: for principal eldest son's wife;

sentences.zh: 為女在室者，為子之為人後者；

translations.literal: for unmarried daughter, for son who becomes heir;
translations.idiomatic: for unmarried daughter, for son who becomes heir;

sentences.zh: 繼母為長子、眾子；

translations.literal: stepmother for eldest and all sons;
translations.idiomatic: stepmother for eldest and all sons;

sentences.zh: 孫為祖父、母；

translations.literal: grandson for grandfather and grandmother;
translations.idiomatic: grandson for grandfather and grandmother;

sentences.zh: 孫女在室、出嫁同；

translations.literal: granddaughter unmarried or married likewise;
translations.idiomatic: granddaughter unmarried or married likewise;

sentences.zh: 女出嫁為父、母；

translations.literal: married daughter for father and mother;
translations.idiomatic: married daughter for father and mother;

sentences.zh: 為人後者為其本生父、母；

translations.literal: heir for birth father and mother;
translations.idiomatic: heir for birth father and mother;

sentences.zh: 女在室或出嫁而無夫與子者為其兄、弟、姊、妹及侄與侄女在室者；

translations.literal: unmarried or married daughter without husband and son for elder and younger brother and sister and unmarried nephew and niece;
translations.idiomatic: daughter without husband and son for siblings and unmarried nephews and nieces;

sentences.zh: 女適人為兄、弟之為父後者；

translations.literal: married daughter for brother who bears the father line;
translations.idiomatic: married daughter for brother bearing the father line;

sentences.zh: 婦為夫兄、弟之子及女在室者；

translations.literal: daughter-in-law for husband's brother's son and unmarried daughter;
translations.idiomatic: daughter-in-law for husband's brother's son and unmarried daughter;

sentences.zh: 妾為家長之父、母與妻及長子、眾子與其所生子。

translations.literal: concubine for householder's father and mother, wife, eldest and all sons, and her own sons.
translations.idiomatic: concubine for householder's parents, wife, sons, and her own sons.

sentences.zh: 曰齊衰五月，為曾祖父、母，女雖適人不降。

translations.literal: Fourth, qi five months—for great-grandfather and great-grandmother; daughter though married does not reduce.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, qi five months—for great-grandparents; married daughter does not reduce.

sentences.zh: 曰齊衰三月，為高祖父、母，女雖適人不降；

translations.literal: Fifth, qi three months—for great-great-grandfather and great-great-grandmother; daughter though married does not reduce;
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, qi three months—for great-great-grandparents; married daughter does not reduce;

sentences.zh: 為繼父昔同居者；

translations.literal: for former stepfather once cohabiting;
translations.idiomatic: for former stepfather once cohabiting;

sentences.zh: 為同居繼父兩有大功以上親者。

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十年，高宗特旨允以獨子兼祧，於是始定兼祧例。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year of Qianlong the Gaozong specially approved by edict that an only son might bear two lines of sacrifice, and from this the precedent for dual-line succession was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 40 Qianlong specially approved that an only son might bear two sacrificial lines, fixing the precedent for dual-line succession.

sentences.zh: 兼祧者從權以濟經，足補古禮之闕。

translations.literal: Dual-line succession used expedient authority to aid the canonical, sufficient to supplement gaps in ancient ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Dual-line succession used expedient means to aid the canonical, supplementing gaps in ancient ritual.

sentences.zh: 會典服制別大宗、小宗，以大宗為重。

translations.literal: The Collected Statutes mourning dress distinguished great descent-line and lesser descent-line, taking the great line as weighty.
translations.idiomatic: The Collected Statutes distinguished great and lesser descent-lines, the great line being weighty.

sentences.zh: 大宗依服制本條持服，兼祧依降服持服。

translations.literal: The great line wore mourning by the garment regulation's main article; dual-line succession wore mourning by reduced grade.
translations.idiomatic: The great line followed the main mourning article; dual-line succession followed reduced mourning.

sentences.zh: 道光九年，禮臣增議兩祧服制，以獨子之子分承兩房宗祧者，各為父、母服斬衰三年，為祖父、母服齊衰不杖期。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang rites officials added deliberation on mourning for two lines: when an only son's son divided to bear two houses' ancestral sacrifices, each wore zhan three years for father and mother and qi without staff one year for grandfather and grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 9 rites officials added two-line mourning: when an only son's son bore two houses, each wore zhan three years for parents and qi one year for grandparents.

sentences.zh: 父故，嫡孫承重，俱服斬衰三年。

translations.literal: When father was dead the principal grandson bore the main line, all wearing zhan three years.
translations.idiomatic: When father was dead the principal grandson bore the main line in zhan three years.

sentences.zh: 其本身為本生親屬俱從正服降一等，子孫為本生親屬祗論所後宗支親屬服制。

translations.literal: For birth kin the person himself all followed proper garment reduced one grade; descendants for birth kin followed only the adopted line's kin garment regulations.
translations.idiomatic: For birth kin he himself reduced one grade from proper mourning; descendants for birth kin followed only the adopted line's regulations.

sentences.zh: 同治十年，允禮臣請，兼祧庶母服制，依定制為兼祧父、母服期，為兼祧庶母服小功。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tongzhi the rites officials' request was approved for mourning dress for a dual-line concubine mother: by regulation mourning for dual-line father and mother was one-year term, for dual-line concubine mother xiao gong.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 10 mourning for a dual-line concubine mother was approved: one-year term for dual-line parents, xiao gong for dual-line concubine mother.

sentences.zh: 其以大宗子兼祧小宗與以小宗兼祧大宗者，以大宗為重。

translations.literal: Whether a great-line son dual-succeeded to a lesser line or a lesser-line son dual-succeeded to the great line, the great line was weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Whether great line dual-succeeded to lesser or lesser to great, the great line was weighty.

sentences.zh: 為大宗庶母服期年，小宗庶母服小功。

translations.literal: For the great line's concubine mother one-year term; for the lesser line's concubine mother xiao gong.
translations.idiomatic: For the great line's concubine mother one year; for the lesser line's xiao gong.

sentences.zh: 其以小宗兼祧小宗者，以所生為重，為本生庶母服期年，為兼祧庶母服小功。

translations.literal: When a lesser-line son dual-succeeded to a lesser line, birth was weighty: for birth concubine mother one-year term, for dual-line concubine mother xiao gong.
translations.idiomatic: When lesser dual-succeeded to lesser, birth was weighty: one year for birth concubine mother, xiao gong for dual-line concubine mother.

sentences.zh: 至出嗣而非兼祧者，以所後為重，為所後庶母服期年，為本生庶母服小功。

translations.literal: For one who went out as heir but was not dual-line, the adopted line was weighty: for adopted concubine mother one-year term, for birth concubine mother xiao gong.
translations.idiomatic: For adoption without dual-line, the adopted line was weighty: one year for adopted concubine mother, xiao gong for birth concubine mother.

sentences.zh: 既降期而服小功，其兼祧庶母為兼祧子持服亦如之。

translations.literal: Since the term was reduced to one year yet xiao gong was worn, the dual-line concubine mother's mourning by the dual-line son was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Since one-year term still used xiao gong, the dual-line son's mourning for the dual-line concubine mother was likewise.
